q.s: Two populations of a species of squirrel are geographically isolated from each other. Although they have the same population density, one population is significantly larger in number than the other. A new bacterial disease, which is easily spread and extremely virulent, affects both populations at the same time. Which of the following is the best prediction of how the new disease will affect the two populations?

o.l: The two populations will be equally affected, because the ability to trigger an immune response is randomly distributed among all squirrels of that species.

The larger population will be less affected by the disease than will the smaller population, because the mutation rate of the larger population is higher than the mutation rate of the smaller population.
The smaller population will be more affected than will the larger population, because the smaller population has less genetic variation than the larger population has.
The smaller population will be less affected than will the larger population, because the smaller population exhibits more genetic drift than the larger population exhibits.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex:
The key concept here is the relationship between population size and genetic diversity. Larger populations maintain greater genetic variation because they experience less genetic drift and have more total alleles present. When a virulent disease strikes, populations with higher genetic diversity are more likely to contain individuals with alleles conferring resistance to the pathogen. The smaller population, having reduced genetic variation due to stronger genetic drift effects and fewer total alleles, is less likely to harbor resistance alleles. This makes the smaller population more vulnerable to being devastated by the disease, as fewer individuals will possess the genetic variants needed to survive infection.

Option i2 is correct because it accurately identifies that the smaller population has less genetic variation than the larger population, making it more susceptible to the disease's effects.

q.s: Mitochondria are found in most eukaryotic cells and contain their own DNA and ribosomes that are similar to those typical of many prokaryotic cells. Which of the following statements is justified by these observations?

o.l: The mitochondrion is the only location in which eukaryotic cells can synthesize ATP.
An ancestral cell most likely engulfed an aerobic prokaryote in a relationship that proved beneficial for both cells.
Mitochondrial membranes provide abundant surface area for reactions because of the infoldings called cristae.
The mitochondrion plays a role in respiration, but it also stores the cell’s extra mRNA.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The presence of mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes similar to prokaryotic cells supports the endosymbiotic theory of mitochondrial origin. This theory proposes that mitochondria evolved from free-living prokaryotic organisms that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells. The retention of their own genetic material and protein synthesis machinery indicates mitochondria were once independent organisms. A mutually beneficial relationship developed where the engulfed prokaryote provided efficient aerobic respiration while receiving protection and nutrients from the host cell. This explains why mitochondria retain prokaryote-like characteristics rather than having typical eukaryotic features. Option i1 is correct because it directly explains the observed similarities between mitochondria and prokaryotes through the endosymbiotic theory.

q.s:
Sickle-cell anemia is associated with a mutation in the gene encoding the beta subunit of hemoglobin that results in a change from glutamic acid to valine at position 6. All other amino acids are identical to a normal hemoglobin molecule.

Based on the information above, which of the following mutations is the most likely cause of sickle-cell anemia?

o.l: A single base-pair substitution in the gene encoding the beta subunit
A single base-pair insertion in the gene encoding the beta subunit
A single base-pair deletion in the gene encoding the beta subunit
A translocation of DNA from one chromosome to another

tg: Skill:Skill 6.C: Provide reasoning to justify a claim by connecting evidence to biological theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The mutation changes only one amino acid (glutamic acid to valine at position 6) while all other amino acids remain identical to normal hemoglobin. A single base-pair substitution, also called a point mutation, changes one nucleotide in the DNA sequence, which alters one codon in the mRNA. This results in the incorporation of a different amino acid at that specific position without affecting the rest of the protein sequence. In contrast, insertions or deletions cause frameshift mutations that would alter all downstream amino acids, and a translocation would likely disrupt the entire gene or its regulation. The correct answer is i0 because only a single base-pair substitution produces the observed effect of changing exactly one amino acid while preserving the rest of the protein sequence.

q.s: In the year 2000, specimens of Caulerpa taxifolia,a green alga used in tropical aquariums, were found off the coast of California. Native to the Indian Ocean, C. taxifolia is known for aggressive growth and an ability to compete with sea grasses.It is currently on an international list of invasive species. Which of the following best predicts the consequences of the introduction of C. taxifolia to the California coast?

o.l: Without natural herbivores or competitors,C. taxifolia will grow rapidly and crowd out native species of producers.
C. taxifolia will have a hard time establishing itself because it will have to compete against native species of sea grasses, which are better adapted to the environment.
C. taxifolia will grow rapidly, leading to an increase in the diversity of producers.
Because it is not in the Indian Ocean, its natural environment, C. taxifolia will not be able to grow efficiently.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex:
The key to this question is understanding the characteristics of invasive species and the information provided about *Caulerpa taxifolia*. The stimulus states that *C. taxifolia* is known for aggressive growth, can compete with sea grasses, and is on an international list of invasive species. Invasive species typically thrive when introduced to new environments because they lack natural predators, herbivores, or competitors that would normally control their populations in their native habitat. Without these natural checks in California waters, *C. taxifolia* would be expected to grow unchecked and outcompete native producers for space and resources, reducing biodiversity rather than increasing it. This pattern is characteristic of successful invasive species worldwide.

Option i0 is correct because it accurately predicts that without natural controls, the invasive alga will grow rapidly and displace native species through competition.

q.s: The graph above represents the number of individuals in a population of wolves and in a population of moose observed in the same isolated geographic area over a 40-year period, from 1955 through 1995. Which of the following statements about the two populations is best supported by the information presented in the graph?

o.l: The reproductive rate of the wolves was greater than the reproductive rate of the moose.
Mutualism allowed the two populations to reproduce while occupying the same ecological niche.
Speciation occurred when the two populations became reproductively isolated from each other.
The wolves were predators of the moose, which were otherwise reproductively successful.

tg: Skill:Skill 2.C: Explain how biological concepts or processes represented visually relate to larger biological principles, concepts, processes or theories.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The graph shows cyclical population dynamics between wolves and moose over 40 years. When the moose population increases (such as from 1958 to 1972, reaching about 1,400), the wolf population subsequently increases (peaking around 1980 at 48 wolves). When wolf numbers are high, moose populations decline (dropping to about 900 by 1982), followed by a decline in wolf numbers (falling to about 12 in 1982). This pattern of predator population changes lagging behind prey population changes is characteristic of predator-prey relationships. The moose population's ability to rebound repeatedly (reaching 2,400 by 1995) demonstrates reproductive success when predation pressure is reduced. Option i3 is correct because it accurately describes the predator-prey relationship shown by the cyclical, inverse correlation between wolf and moose populations, where wolves control but do not eliminate the reproductively successful moose population.

q.s: Which of the following statements is best supported by the data?

o.l: Black bears are a keystone species.
Salmon are a keystone species.
Black bear urine is a significant source of nitrogen in the environment.
The presence of black bears and salmon correlates with a significant increase in nitrogen influx.

f.c:
Pacific salmon and black bears have often been cited as examples of keystone species. Pacific salmon spawn in freshwater streams but spend most of their lives at sea. When mature salmon return to the freshwater streams to spawn, they are preyed upon by bears and other predators. When salmon migrate from their marine habitat to the freshwater streams, they bring nitrogen and other marine-derived nutrients that subsequently remain in the areas surrounding the streams—a process called nitrogen influx.

In an investigation, the relationship between black bears, salmon, and influx of marine nitrogen into the area around a southwestern Alaskan stream was studied. The investigators established several test plots of the same size along the stream with the following species composition: no salmon or black bears (N), bears but not salmon (B), salmon but not bears (S), and a plot where salmon and bears interact (SB). Nitrogen influx in the different sampling areas was measured as a means of assessing the impact of the different species on the health of the ecosystem. The data are plotted in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Mean nitrogen influx  as a function of species present. N = neither salmon nor bears present, B = only bears present, S = only salmon present and SB = both salmon and bears present.

tg: Skill:Skill 2.B: Explain relationships between different characteristics of biological concepts or processes represented visually- a. In theoretical contexts. b. In applied contexts.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The question asks which statement is best supported by data (presumably showing nitrogen levels in environments with and without bears and salmon). A keystone species is defined as one whose removal dramatically alters ecosystem structure, but the data likely only shows correlation with nitrogen levels, not evidence of ecosystem-wide structural changes from removal. While bear urine may contribute nitrogen, calling it "significant" requires comparing it to other nitrogen sources, which the data presumably doesn't address comprehensively. The correct answer identifies a correlation between the presence of both black bears and salmon with increased nitrogen influx, which is a direct observational claim that data measuring nitrogen levels in different conditions would support. Option i3 is correct because it makes a specific, measurable claim about correlation that can be directly verified by comparing nitrogen measurements across different environmental conditions without requiring additional ecological assumptions.

q.ex: Bears catch salmon from rivers and consume them, often carrying portions away from the water to eat. Salmon are rich in marine-derived nitrogen because they spend years feeding in the ocean before returning to freshwater to spawn. As decomposition occurs, this nitrogen is released into the soil, enriching the terrestrial ecosystem. This process represents a significant transfer of nutrients from marine to terrestrial environments. Option i0 is correct because it accurately describes this nutrient transfer mechanism where bear feeding behavior facilitates the movement and release of nitrogen from salmon into the surrounding environment through decomposition.

q.ex: To investigate the relationship between bears, salmon, and nitrogen influx, researchers need to track how nitrogen from salmon enters the ecosystem. The other options either disrupt the natural system being studied or don't directly measure the bear-salmon-nitrogen transfer pathway. Option i0 is correct because it provides direct quantitative data on the nitrogen transfer mechanism while maintaining the natural bear-salmon interaction.

q.ex: When salmon migrate upstream, they bring marine-derived nitrogen into terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems. Bears catch salmon and transport them into forests, where the fish carcasses decompose and release nitrogen into the soil. If a dam blocks salmon migration, salmon cannot reach the test sites upstream. Without salmon present, bears cannot transport salmon-derived nitrogen into the ecosystem, resulting in decreased nitrogen influx to those areas. The correct answer is that nitrogen influx will decrease because there will be less bear-salmon interaction, as the absence of migrating salmon eliminates this critical pathway for nitrogen transfer from marine to terrestrial environments.

q.s: As depicted in the diagram, honeybees communicate the location of flower patches to members of their hives with waggle dances that give information about the direction and distance to the flowers. Which of the following statements about how honeybees communicate the position of flower patches is most consistent with the model?

o.l: The number of repetitions of the waggle dance indicates the quality of the pollen source.
The total area covered by any waggle dance leads bees to the target flowers.
The angle of the waggle phase relative to the vertical plane indicates the position of the target flowers relative to another beehive.
The farther the target flowers from the hive, the longer the waggle phase.

tg: Skill:Skill 2.C: Explain how biological concepts or processes represented visually relate to larger biological principles, concepts, processes or theories.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The waggle dance encodes distance and direction information through specific components. In the left hive example, the flower patch is 500 meters away and the waggle phase lasts 375 milliseconds. In the right hive example, the flower patch is 160 meters away and the waggle phase lasts 150 milliseconds. The ratio shows that greater distance corresponds to longer waggle phase duration (500m/375ms versus 160m/150ms both yield approximately 1.33 m/ms). The angle of the waggle dance indicates direction relative to the sun, not to another hive, and the stimulus provides no information about dance repetitions or total area covered relating to the target location. Option i3 is correct because it accurately describes the relationship demonstrated in the model: increased distance to flowers correlates with increased duration of the waggle phase.

Some strains of the bacterium Streptococcus pyogenes secrete poisonous substances called exotoxins. The genes encoding the exotoxins are thought to have originated in bacteriophages, which are viruses that infect bacteria.

Which of the following is the most likely mechanism by which the S. pyogenes acquired the ability to produce the exotoxins?

o.l: Bacteriophages engulfed cellular debris from dead bacteria.
Bacteriophages in the environment activated bacterial cell division.

Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The question asks how bacteria acquired genes from bacteriophages that allow them to produce exotoxins. Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria and can transfer genetic material through a process called transduction. When bacteriophage DNA integrates into the bacterial chromosome, the viral genes become a permanent part of the bacterial genome and can be expressed by the bacterium. This horizontal gene transfer mechanism allows bacteria to acquire new traits, including the ability to produce toxins encoded by viral genes. Options involving engulfment, cell division activation, or protein absorption do not explain how the genes themselves were acquired and passed on. Option i2 is correct because integration of bacteriophage DNA into the bacterial chromosome is the established mechanism by which bacteria permanently acquire and express viral genes.

q.ex: In speciation models, when populations diverge genetically due to geographic isolation or other factors, hybrids formed between these diverging populations often have reduced fitness compared to pure individuals from either parent population. This reduced fitness can result from genetic incompatibilities, developmental abnormalities, or reduced ability to survive and reproduce in either parental environment. Over time, natural selection acts against these less-fit hybrids, meaning they are less successful at surviving to reproductive age and producing viable offspring. This process reinforces reproductive isolation between the diverging populations and is a key mechanism in completing speciation. Option i0 is correct because it accurately describes how hybrids typically have lower reproductive success, making them less likely to pass their genes to future generations.

q.ex: When calculating allele frequencies for populations undergoing speciation, only individuals that can reproduce and pass their alleles to the next generation should be included in the calculations. Hybrid males at intermediate stages of speciation are often sterile due to genetic incompatibilities between the two diverging populations, a phenomenon known as Haldane's rule in many species. Since sterile individuals cannot produce offspring, their genotypes do not contribute alleles to future generations and including them would artificially skew the calculated allele frequencies. The correct answer is that sterile individuals make no genetic contribution to the next generation, which is why hybrid males must be excluded from allele frequency calculations if they are reproductively unviable.

q.ex: The key to this question is identifying the degree of reproductive isolation between the two populations. The populations can produce hybrid offspring when mated in the laboratory, indicating they are not completely reproductively isolated. However, the hybrids show reduced fertility—only females are fertile, while males are sterile. This partial sterility in hybrids is a classic example of Haldane's rule and indicates incomplete reproductive isolation. The populations have begun diverging genetically but have not yet reached complete speciation. This pattern of partial hybrid sterility is characteristic of an intermediate stage of speciation, where prezygotic barriers are weak or absent but postzygotic barriers (reduced hybrid fitness) are developing. The intermediate stage represents populations that are in the process of diverging but can still interbreed with reduced success.

q.ex: In species where males are homogametic (ZZ) and females are heterogametic (ZW), such as birds and butterflies, Haldane's rule predicts that the heterogametic sex will show reduced fitness or sterility first during hybridization. This occurs because recessive deleterious alleles on the Z chromosome are immediately expressed in the heterogametic (ZW) females, while homogametic (ZZ) males can mask these alleles with a functional copy on their second Z chromosome. During speciation, when populations diverge and hybrids form, genetic incompatibilities accumulate faster in the sex with only one copy of sex-linked genes. Therefore, sterility would appear in females before appearing in males, making option i0 correct because it directly applies Haldane's rule to a ZW sex determination system.

q.s:
A scientist is evaluating a proposal for raising large numbers of fish in ocean pens for human consumption. As part of the evaluation, the scientist is designing a plan for investigating how the fish in the ocean pens might affect nearby ecosystems.

Which of the following is the most appropriate factor to use as the dependent variable in the experimental investigation?

o.l: The amount of metabolic wastes in the water where the fish are being raised
The water temperature in the natural habitat of the fish being studied
The types of fish that are preferentially consumed by humans
The amount of time it takes for fish to digest a meal

tg: Skill:Skill 3.C: Identify experimental procedures that are aligned to the question, including- a. Identifying dependent and independent variables. b. Identifying appropriate controls. c. Justifying appropriate controls.
Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: The dependent variable is what the scientist measures to assess the effect of the independent variable. In this investigation, the independent variable is the presence of fish in ocean pens, and the scientist wants to determine how these pens affect nearby ecosystems. The amount of metabolic wastes in the water is a measurable outcome that would directly indicate the impact of the fish pens on the surrounding environment. Water temperature, human consumption preferences, and digestion time are either unrelated to ecosystem impact or not outcomes that would change as a result of the fish pens. The correct answer is the amount of metabolic wastes in the water because it is the measured response variable that indicates how the fish pens affect the nearby ecosystem.

q.s: Epinephrine is a protein hormone found in many animals. Epinephrine stimulates a signaling pathway that results in the breakdown of glycogen to glucose in the liver cells. Which of the following describes the initial steps in the process whereby epinephrine stimulates glycogen breakdown?

o.l: Epinephrine binds to a cell-surface receptor; the activated receptor stimulates production of the second messenger, cAMP MathType@MTEF@5@5@+=feaagCart1ev2aaatCvAUfeBSjuyZL2yd9gzLbvyNv2CaerbuLwBLnhiov2DGi1BTfMBaeXatLxBI9gBaerbd9wDYLwzYbItLDharqqtubsr4rNCHbGeaGqiVu0Je9sqqrpepC0xbbL8F4rqqrFfpeea0xe9Lq=Jc9vqaqpepm0xbba9pwe9Q8fs0=yqaqpepae9pg0FirpepeKkFr0xfr=xfr=xb9adbaqaaeGaciGaaiaabeqaamaabaabaaGcbaGaae4yaiaabgeacaqGnbGaaeiuaaaa@3941@ .
Epinephrine binds to a cell-surface receptor; the activated receptor catalyzes the conversion of glycogen to glucose.
Epinephrine diffuses through the plasma membrane; the hormone dimerizes in the cytosol.
Epinephrine is taken into the cell by endocytosis; glycogen is converted to glucose in the endocytotic vesicle.

tg: Skill:Skill 1.B: Explain biological concepts and/or processes.
Practice:Practice 1: Explain Biological Concepts, Processes, and Models Presented in Written Format.
q.ex: Epinephrine is a protein hormone, which means it is hydrophilic and cannot cross the lipid bilayer of the plasma membrane. Instead, it must bind to a cell-surface receptor on the outside of liver cells. Upon binding, the receptor undergoes a conformational change that activates intracellular signaling pathways. This activation stimulates the enzyme adenylyl cyclase, which converts ATP to cyclic AMP (cAMP), a crucial second messenger. The cAMP then triggers a cascade of events leading to glycogen breakdown. Option i0 is correct because it accurately describes this receptor-mediated signaling mechanism where epinephrine binds externally and initiates cAMP production as the second messenger.

Which molecular substance is actively transported across the plasma membrane?
How does temperature affect the movement of molecules into lysosomes?

Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: The figure depicts three different types of membrane transport: simple diffusion (white circles moving directly through the lipid bilayer), facilitated diffusion (black rectangles moving through a channel protein from high to low concentration), and active transport (black ovals moving through a carrier protein against their concentration gradient, from low to high concentration). The key distinguishing feature is that the black ovals on the right move from a region of lower concentration (extracellular fluid) to higher concentration (cytosol), which requires energy input and represents active transport. Option i2 directly asks which substance undergoes active transport, making it the most relevant question to the model shown. The correct answer is i2 because it specifically addresses the identification of actively transported molecules, which is clearly demonstrated by the rightmost transport mechanism in the figure.

q.s:
A group of students designed an experiment to determine the effect of compost on the germination and growth of plants. The students set up experimental plots by mixing different ratios of soil and compost. They planted 20 pea and 20 melon seeds in each plot and watered each plot regularly. The students recorded the number of seeds that germinated, and as the plants grew, they recorded plant length, number and size of leaves, and general health observations.

The following observations were recorded.

  • In all treatments, more pea seeds germinated than melon seeds.
  • There was a week of rainy weather at three weeks.
  • Melon plants developed a fungal growth at four weeks.
  • Melon plants grew longer than pea plants, but many melon leaves showed signs of yellowing as the weeks passed.

The students concluded that pea plants grew better in compost than did melon plants.

Which of the following best addresses the validity of the conclusion made by the students?

o.l: The conclusion is valid because the independent and dependent variables in the experiment were controlled.
The conclusion is valid because the experimental design included a large sample size.
The conclusion is invalid because other variables in the experiment (both biotic and abiotic) affected the results.
The conclusion is invalid because the units of measurement were not given in the experimental design.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The students' conclusion is flawed because multiple uncontrolled variables confounded the results. The rainy weather at three weeks introduced an uncontrolled abiotic variable that could have affected both plant types differently. The fungal growth on melon plants at four weeks represents an uncontrolled biotic variable that likely impaired melon growth and health, as evidenced by the yellowing leaves. These confounding factors make it impossible to attribute the differences in plant performance solely to the compost treatment. A valid experiment requires controlling or accounting for extraneous variables to isolate the effect of the independent variable (compost ratio) on the dependent variables (germination and growth). The conclusion is invalid because other variables affected the results, making option i2 correct.

q.s: Butterflies of the genus Colias live in the Rocky Mountains, where they experience a wide range of temperatures. Different variants of a particular glycolytic enzyme in the flight muscles are optimally active at different temperatures. Within the same population, some individual butterflies fly most effectively at 29°C , while others fly most effectively at 40°C. Still others can be equally active at both temperatures. Which of the following claims is most consistent with the observed butterfly behavior?

o.l: Butterflies that express two variants of the enzyme are active over a greater range of temperature.
Butterflies that are active over a wide range of temperatures produce greater amounts of the enzyme.
Temperature has little effect on the activity of butterflies.
Butterflies that are active at warmer temperatures produce more offspring.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.
Topic:3.3: Environmental Impacts on Enzyme Function
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The question describes butterflies with different enzyme variants that function optimally at different temperatures (29°C or 40°C), while some individuals are equally active at both temperatures. This pattern suggests genetic variation in the enzyme, where some butterflies are homozygous for one variant, others are homozygous for the other variant, and some are heterozygous. Butterflies that are heterozygous would express both enzyme variants simultaneously, allowing them to maintain flight muscle activity across a broader temperature range since one variant works well at lower temperatures and the other at higher temperatures. This explains why some individuals fly effectively at both 29°C and 40°C. Option i0 is correct because butterflies expressing two enzyme variants (heterozygotes) would indeed be active over a greater temperature range than those expressing only one variant.

tg: Topic:7.13: Origins of Life on Earth
Skill:Skill 3.D: Make observations or collect data from representations of laboratory setups or results.
Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: These experiments recreate the Miller-Urey experiment, which demonstrated abiotic synthesis of organic molecules under early Earth conditions. The key to forming molecular building blocks like amino acids is having sources of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen that can be energized by spark discharge to form complex organic molecules. Experiment 1 contains nitrogen gas (N2) and ammonia (NH3), both of which provide nitrogen atoms that are essential components of amino acids. When energized by electrical sparks simulating lightning, these nitrogen sources can combine with carbon from methane (CH4) and other elements to synthesize amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. Option i1 is correct because nitrogen availability from N2 and NH3 in Experiment 1 enables amino acid formation, which are fundamental molecular building blocks essential for life.

The validity of the cladogram is best supported by molecular evidence for which of the following changes in the amino acid composition of the beta-hemoglobin protein during the evolution of these species?

There was no relationship between days without food and average brood size.

f.c:
Diapause is the interruption of an organism’s life cycle in response to environmental cues. The soil nematode Caenorhabditis elegans is capable of entering adult reproductive diapause ( ARD MathType@MTEF@5@5@+=feaagCart1ev2aaatCvAUfeBSjuyZL2yd9gzLbvyNv2CaerbuLwBLnhiov2DGi1BTfMBaeXatLxBI9gBaerbd9wDYLwzYbItLDharqqtubsr4rNCHbGeaGqiVu0Je9sqqrpepC0xbbL8F4rqqrFfpeea0xe9Lq=Jc9vqaqpepm0xbba9pwe9Q8fs0=yqaqpepae9pg0FirpepeKkFr0xfr=xfr=xb9adbaqaaeGaciGaaiaabeqaamaabaabaaGcbaGaaeyqaiaabkfacaqGebaaaa@3854@ ) when food is scarce. In C. elegans, individuals normally become reproductively mature 2 days after hatching and remain fertile for 18 days. q.ex: To determine the average brood size per mated individual after 30 days of ARD (adult reproductive diapause), we need to analyze the data from the reintroduction experiment. When food is reintroduced following a period of reproductive arrest, organisms typically resume reproduction at rates characteristic of their species under favorable conditions. For many model organisms like C. elegans or Drosophila commonly used in such studies, the average brood size per mated individual after recovery from diapause typically ranges from 40-60 offspring. Among the given options (10, 50, 250, 400), values of 250 or 400 would represent exceptionally high fecundity seen only in highly prolific species under optimal conditions, while 10 would indicate severely compromised reproduction. The value of 50 represents a moderate, biologically realistic brood size consistent with recovery from temporary reproductive arrest. The correct answer is 50 because it reflects typical post-diapause reproductive output for organisms in controlled laboratory reintro

Diapause is the interruption of an organism’s life cycle in response to environmental cues. The soil nematode Caenorhabditis elegans is capable of entering adult reproductive diapause ( ARD MathType@MTEF@5@5@+=feaagCart1ev2aaatCvAUfeBSjuyZL2yd9gzLbvyNv2CaerbuLwBLnhiov2DGi1BTfMBaeXatLxBI9gBaerbd9wDYLwzYbItLDharqqtubsr4rNCHbGeaGqiVu0Je9sqqrpepC0xbbL8F4rqqrFfpeea0xe9Lq=Jc9vqaqpepm0xbba9pwe9Q8fs0=yqaqpepae9pg0FirpepeKkFr0xfr=xfr=xb9adbaqaaeGaciGaaiaabeqaamaabaabaaGcbaGaaeyqaiaabkfacaqGebaaaa@3854@ ) when food is scarce. In C. elegans, individuals normally become reproductively mature 2 days after hatching and remain fertile for 18 days. They reproduce either by self-fertilization or by mating with another individual.

q.ex: ARD (adult reproductive diapause) is an evolutionary adaptation that allows C. elegans to pause reproduction during unfavorable conditions like food scarcity. The key evolutionary concept here is selective advantage—traits persist in populations when they increase survival or reproductive success under environmental pressures. Option i0 correctly identifies that ARD provides a selective advantage by enabling reproduction to occur despite periods of food scarcity, meaning organisms can survive harsh conditions and reproduce when resources return. This differs from option i1, which incorrectly suggests ARD individuals produce more offspring overall, and option i3, which uses "high fitness" without explaining the mechanism. Option i2 focuses on longevity rather than reproductive success, which is less relevant to evolutionary fitness. Option i0 is correct because it accurately describes how ARD confers selective advantage through reproductive flexibility during environmental stress.

q.ex: The diagram shows that steroid hormone signaling promotes transcription of a specific gene, which produces target-gene mRNA that is then translated into proteins. When the hormone-receptor complex binds to DNA, it acts as a transcription factor that increases transcription of that particular gene. This directly results in increased production of the specific mRNA corresponding to that gene. Option i0 is incorrect because histone synthesis is not a direct consequence of activating one specific gene. Option i1 is wrong because ribosomes are not specific to particular mRNAs and their production would not necessarily increase from activating a single gene. Option i2 is incorrect because the hormone-receptor complex promotes transcription, not DNA replication. Option i3 is correct because increased transcription of a specific gene directly produces more of that gene's mRNA.

tg: Skill:Skill 2.C: Explain how biological concepts or processes represented visually relate to larger biological principles, concepts, processes or theories.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The key to this question is understanding mitochondrial inheritance patterns. Mitochondrial DNA is inherited exclusively through the maternal line because the egg contributes nearly all cytoplasm (and thus mitochondria) to the zygote, while sperm contribute almost none. If this trait were mitochondrial, every offspring of an affected mother would inherit the trait. However, the pedigree shows affected mothers (shaded circles) having unaffected offspring (unshaded symbols) in multiple generations, which contradicts strict maternal inheritance. For example, in Generation 2, the affected mother on the right has both affected and unaffected children, and in Generation 3, an affected mother produces both affected and unaffected offspring. This pattern is consistent with nuclear inheritance where offspring can inherit different alleles, but inconsistent with mitochondrial inheritance where all maternal offspring must be affected. Option i2 is correct because it accurately states the defining characteristic of mitochondrial inheritance that is violated in this pedigree.

q.ex: An ethical question concerns moral principles, values, and societal implications rather than purely scientific or medical facts. Option i0 addresses the medical utility of testing, which is a practical consideration. Option i1 asks about eliminating alleles from cells, which is a technical/scientific question about feasibility. Option i3 inquires about available treatments, which is a medical information question. Option i2 raises concerns about genetic discrimination and whether insurance companies should use genetic test results to adjust rates, which directly involves moral considerations about privacy, fairness, and the potential misuse of genetic information. This represents a genuine ethical dilemma about how genetic data should be used in society. Option i2 is correct because it addresses the moral implications of genetic testing rather than technical or medical aspects.

The cell continues to transcribe the genes that code for the hydrolytic enzymes that are normally found in lysosomes and continues to translate the mRNAs MathType@MTEF@5@5@+=feaagCart1ev2aaatCvAUfeBSjuyZL2yd9gzLbvyNv2CaerbuLwBLnhiov2DGi1BTfMBaeXatLxBI9gBaerbd9wDYLwzYbItLDharqqtubsr4rNCHbGeaGqiVu0Je9sqqrpepC0xbbL8F4rqqrFfpeea0xe9Lq=Jc9vqaqpepm0xbba9pwe9Q8fs0=yqaqpepae9pg0FirpepeKkFr0xfr=xfr=xb9adbaqaaeGaciGaaiaabeqaamaabaabaaGcbaGaaeyBaiaabkfacaqGobGaaeyqaiaabohaaaa@3A44@ for those proteins on membrane-bound ribosomes.

The hydrolytic enzymes are most likely to accumulate in which of the following cellular structures?

o.l: Nucleus
Mitochondrion
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
Golgi complex

tg: Skill:Skill 1.A: Describe biological concepts and/or processes.
Practice:Practice 1: Explain Biological Concepts, Processes, and Models Presented in Written Format.
q.ex: The hydrolytic enzymes destined for lysosomes are synthesized on membrane-bound ribosomes and enter the rough endoplasmic reticulum. From the RER, these proteins are transported to the Golgi complex for processing, sorting, and packaging. Normally, the Golgi would package these enzymes into vesicles that become lysosomes. However, since the drug prevents new lysosome formation, the enzymes cannot be packaged into their final destination. The hydrolytic enzymes will therefore accumulate in the Golgi complex, where they are processed and sorted but cannot be properly packaged and released as lysosomes. The correct answer is the Golgi complex because it is the last stop in the secretory pathway before lysosome formation, which has been blocked.

Topic:6.6: Gene Expression and Cell Specialization
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The diagram shows that DNA damage triggers phosphorylation of p53 through a protein kinase cascade. The phosphorylated p53 then binds to the p21 gene, stimulating its transcription and subsequent translation into p21 protein. The p21 protein converts active cyclin-Cdk complexes into inactive forms, which halts cell division. This mechanism allows the cell to pause the cell cycle, providing time for DNA repair before division proceeds. Option i1 correctly describes this pathway where phosphorylated p53 acts as a transcription factor for p21, and p21 suppresses cell division by inactivating cyclin-Cdk complexes until DNA damage is repaired.

q.ex: The question asks for the most appropriate graph to represent experimental results from a table (not shown). Option i1 presents a bar graph with treatment groups 1-6 on the x-axis and mean pH on the y-axis, with error bars included. This format is standard for displaying categorical experimental groups with continuous measurement data. The bar graph allows direct comparison of mean pH values across different treatment groups, while error bars indicate variability or uncertainty in the measurements. A pie chart (i0) is inappropriate for pH measurements, a line graph (i2) incorrectly suggests continuity between discrete treatment groups, and option i3 plots standard error against mean pH rather than showing treatment effects. Option i1 is correct because bar graphs with error bars are the standard way to display mean values of a continuous variable across distinct experimental treatment groups.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex:
During photosynthesis, plants consume carbon dioxide from the water, which reduces the concentration of dissolved CO2. Since CO2 in water forms carbonic acid (H2CO3), removing CO2 decreases the acidity of the solution, causing the pH to increase. An increase in mean pH after one hour directly indicates that CO2 was being removed from the water by the aquatic plants. This CO2 uptake is a key component of photosynthesis, where plants use CO2, water, and light energy to produce glucose and oxygen. The other options describe experimental conditions or statistical measures but do not provide direct evidence that the photosynthetic process actually occurred.

The correct choice is correct because an increase in pH demonstrates CO2 consumption, which is direct evidence of photosynthetic activity.

q.ex: To determine if an organism can perform both photosynthesis and respiration, you need to test it under conditions that allow each process separately. Photosynthesis requires light and produces oxygen, while respiration consumes oxygen and occurs in both light and dark conditions. Treatment I likely represents a light condition where photosynthesis can occur, while Treatment II likely represents a dark condition where only respiration occurs. By comparing oxygen production or consumption in light versus dark, you can identify whether the organism photosynthesizes (net oxygen production in light) and respires (oxygen consumption in dark). This comparison isolates each metabolic process under controlled conditions. The correct choice is I and II because these treatments provide the necessary light and dark conditions to distinguish between photosynthesis and respiration.

q.ex: To determine what question the results from treatment groups V and VI suggest, we need to consider what these groups likely represent as controls or experimental conditions. Treatment group V typically represents a control with just water and light, while treatment VI represents a dark control with just water. If these groups show unexpected changes in pH or dissolved oxygen, it would indicate biological activity occurring in the water itself. The presence of living microorganisms in the aquarium water would explain any metabolic activity (respiration or photosynthesis) observed in these control groups. This is a fundamental experimental design question because uncontrolled microbial populations could confound the results of the entire experiment. The correct answer is option i3 because unexpected results in water-only controls would raise questions about whether living organisms are present in the supposedly abiotic control treatments.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.B: Use confidence intervals and/or error bars (both determined using standard errors) to determine whether sample means are statistically different.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The standard error of the mean (SEM) measures the precision of a sample mean as an estimate of the population mean. It is calculated as SEM = standard deviation / √n, where n is the sample size. To reduce standard error, researchers can either decrease variability in measurements or increase sample size. Since the question asks about modifications to experimental design rather than controlling inherent biological variability, increasing sample size is the most direct and reliable method. Changing water sources (pond vs. aquarium) or exposure time would not systematically reduce standard error and might actually introduce additional variability. Increasing the sample size of each treatment group is correct because it directly decreases the denominator in the SEM calculation, making the standard error smaller and the mean estimates more precise.

q.s:
Many human cells can be stimulated to divide by hormonelike growth factors that bind to receptor proteins (R) on the plasma membrane and trigger an internal signal-transduction cascade. In many cases, however, the process of contact inhibition prevents mitosis when cells are in direct contact with one another. Topic:4.4: Changes in Signal Transduction Pathways
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: The stimulus explains that protein M normally replaces growth-factor signaling proteins when CAMs interact during contact inhibition, thereby preventing cell division. If M function is interrupted, protein 3 would remain associated with CAMs even when cells are in contact, allowing the signal transduction cascade to continue through ras to trigger cell division. This means the cell would divide despite being in direct contact with neighboring cells, overriding the normal contact inhibition mechanism. Uncontrolled cell division despite contact with other cells is a hallmark of cancer. q.ex: The expected results assume a 1:1:1:1 ratio (862 each), which would occur if the two genes assorted independently. However, the observed results show a significant deviation: the parental phenotypes (tan/wild-type and black/vestigial) appear much more frequently (1447 and 1416) than the recombinant phenotypes (tan/vestigial and black/wild-type at 309 and 277). This pattern indicates genetic linkage, where genes located close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together rather than assorting independently. The small number of recombinants results from crossing over between the two loci during meiosis. The correct answer is that the genes for body color and wing shape are located close to each other on the same chromosome, which explains why parental combinations predominate over recombinant types.

q.s:
Some cells release active signaling proteins when membrane-bound precursor proteins are cleaved by proteolytic enzymes. The signaling proteins can then bind to receptors on the surface of a target cell, thereby activating an intracellular signaling pathway and eliciting a response from the target cell.

This mechanism of activating receptor-binding signaling proteins has been observed in a variety of organisms from bacteria to humans. Many of the enzymes responsible for proteolysis of membrane-bound precursor proteins have been isolated and characterized.

Which of the following questions would be most appropriate to investigate whether the proteolytic enzymes are evolutionarily conserved among species?

o.l: Are the genes encoding the proteolytic enzymes expressed in the same cell types in all species?
Once the precursor proteins of different species are cleaved, do the active signaling proteins bind to the same receptors on different target cells?
If a proteolytic enzyme from one species is incubated with a precursor protein from another species, does correct cleavage occur?
Are the proteolytic enzymes synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum of all species?

tg: Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: To determine if proteolytic enzymes are evolutionarily conserved among species, we need to test whether the enzymes from different species retain similar structure and function. Option i2 directly tests functional conservation by examining whether an enzyme from one species can recognize and correctly cleave a substrate from another species. If the enzyme successfully performs the correct cleavage across species boundaries, this indicates that both the enzyme's active site and the substrate's cleavage site have been conserved through evolution. Options i0 and i3 address expression patterns and synthesis location, which do not directly test conservation of enzyme function. Option i1 examines receptor-ligand interactions rather than enzyme conservation. Option i2 is correct because cross-species functional compatibility is the most direct evidence of evolutionary conservation of enzyme structure and function.

q.ex: The table shows that uric acid has very low solubility and requires very low amounts of water for excretion, while ammonia requires high amounts of water. Birds and reptiles primarily produce uric acid as their nitrogenous waste. This adaptation allows these organisms to conserve water effectively, which is particularly important for terrestrial animals and those that lay eggs on land. The statement about reptile and bird kidneys being highly efficient due to minimal water requirements for uric acid excretion directly aligns with the data showing uric acid requires very low water amounts. Option i1 is correct because it accurately connects the low water requirement for uric acid excretion with the efficiency of the excretory system in birds and reptiles.

q.ex: The question establishes that CDK5 requires p35 to be active, meaning CDK5 activity depends on p35 availability. In neurons, CDK5 is involved in various regulatory processes including synaptic function. If p35 is degraded, CDK5 cannot be activated, which would reduce CDK5 activity. However, the correct answer states that degradation of p35 increases synaptic activity, suggesting that CDK5 normally acts as an inhibitor or negative regulator of synaptic activity. When p35 is degraded, CDK5 becomes inactive, removing this inhibitory effect and allowing synaptic activity to increase. This represents a regulatory mechanism where p35 degradation serves as a molecular switch to modulate neuronal signaling. The correct choice is i1 because it correctly predicts that removing the activator protein p35 through degradation would decrease CDK5 activity, thereby releasing its inhibitory control and increasing synaptic activity.

q.ex: The range of responses to a stimulus depends on the ability of the nervous system to produce graded or variable outputs rather than just all-or-none responses. Different neurons releasing different amounts of neurotransmitter allows for quantitative variation in signal strength across a neural network. This means some neurons can release small amounts for weak responses while others release larger amounts for strong responses, creating a spectrum of possible outcomes. Option i0 describes baseline activity but not response variation. Option i2 incorrectly places control at the postsynaptic level during depolarization when neurotransmitter binding is determined by presynaptic release. Option i3 describes degradation after signaling, not the regulation of release that modulates response intensity. The correct answer is i1 because differential neurotransmitter release across neurons directly enables varied response magnitudes to stimuli.

q.ex: The graph shows that when herbivores are present (solid line), the distribution is narrower and peaks around 90 spines, while without herbivores (dashed line), the distribution is broader and includes plants with both fewer and more spines. The key observation is that the presence of herbivores eliminates cacti at both extremes of the spine distribution. This pattern indicates that one herbivore preferentially consumes cacti with fewer spines while the other targets cacti with more spines, leaving only the intermediate spine counts to survive. Peccaries, being large mammals, would find cacti with fewer spines easier to eat, while wasp larvae would have easier access to deposit eggs and feed on cacti with more spines where there is less physical defense. Option i1 is correct because it explains how two different herbivores with opposite preferences create selective pressure that narrows the distribution to favor intermediate spine numbers.

q.ex: In Cross 1, blue male × blue female produces all blue females but a 1:1 ratio of blue to white males, indicating the trait is X-linked with blue dominant. Cross 2 confirms this: blue male × white female yields all blue females (inheriting the blue X from father) and all white males (inheriting the white X from mother). Cross 3 shows white male × blue female producing a 1:1 ratio in both sexes, consistent with X-linked inheritance where the heterozygous blue female passes either allele to offspring. The key evidence is Cross 2, where the complete absence of blue males occurs because males inherit their single X chromosome from the white mother, proving blue is X-linked dominant. Option i3 correctly identifies this pattern.

q.ex: In Population 1, the R allele frequency dropped from 0.3 to 0.0 over 30 years, representing complete loss of this allele. Since the populations are described as small and randomly mating, this dramatic change is most consistent with genetic drift, where random sampling effects in small populations can cause allele frequencies to fluctuate and even result in fixation or loss of alleles. Population 2 shows the opposite trend with R increasing from 0.37 to 0.75, which contradicts Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (which requires constant allele frequencies) and suggests directional selection rather than drift. The loss of one allele does not necessarily lead to extinction since the population can survive with only the r allele. Option i0 is correct because the complete loss of allele R in the small Population 1 is characteristic of genetic drift's random effects on allele frequencies.

q.s: Based on an analysis of the data, identify the preferred host of the forest form and of the domestic form of the mosquito.

f.c:
The yellow-fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is a major vector of human disease. In a particular location in Africa, there are two forms of the mosquito. The forest form of the mosquito is black and often lays its eggs in tree holes and pools of water in the forest. The domestic form of the mosquito is brown and prefers to lay its eggs in rainwater collected near human dwellings.

Researchers used a choice chamber (Figure 1) to investigate the host preference of A. aegypti. The researchers recorded the number of forest-form and domestic-form mosquitoes that bit human or guinea pig hosts during several ten-minute trials. The researchers used these data to calculate a hostpreference index for each form, as shown in Figure 2. Researchers also identified a gene in the mosquitoes, OR4, that encodes an olfactory receptor. A volatile odorant, sulcatone, binds to the OR4 receptor. Humans produce higher levels of sulcatone than do guinea pigs.

q.s:
In a certain flock of sheep, 4 percent of the population has black wool and 96 percent has white wool. Assume that the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

What percentage of the population is homozygous for white wool?
tg: Skill:Skill 5.A: Perform mathematical calculations, including- a. Mathematical equations in the curriculum. b. Means. c. Rates. d. Ratios. e. Percentages.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: In Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of homozygous recessive individuals (black wool) equals q². Since 4 percent have black wool, q² = 0.04, so q = 0.2. Using p + q = 1, the frequency of the dominant allele is p = 0.8. The frequency of homozygous dominant individuals (white wool) is p² = (0.8)² = 0.64 or 64 percent. Note that heterozygotes (2pq = 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.32 or 32 percent) also have white wool due to dominance, but the question specifically asks for homozygous white wool individuals. The correct answer is 64 percent because it represents the frequency of the homozygous dominant genotype.

f.c:
Figure 1. Comet assay to detect double-stranded breaks in DNA

 

A comet assay is a technique used to determine the amount of double-strand breaks in DNA (DNA damage) in cells. The nucleus of an individual cell is placed on a microscope slide coated with an agarose gel. An electric current is applied to the gel that causes DNA to move (electrophoresis), and the DNA is stained with a fluorescent dye. When viewed using a microscope, undamaged DNA from the nucleus appears as a round shape (the head), and the fragments of damaged DNA extend out from the head (the tail). The length of the tail corresponds to the amount of the damage in the DNA (see Figure 1).

q.s: Identify the biochemical pathway S. mutans uses for metabolizing sugar and describe how the pathway contributes to the low pH in the inner layers of plaque.

f.c:
Many species of bacteria grow in the mouths of animals and can form biofilms on teeth (plaque). Within plaque, the outer layers contain high levels of oxygen and the layers closest to the tooth contain low levels of oxygen. The surface of the tooth is covered in a hard layer of enamel, which can be dissolved under acidic conditions. When the enamel breaks down, the bacteria in plaque can extract nutrients from the tooth and cause cavities.

Certain types of bacteria (e.g., Streptococcus mutans) thrive in the innermost anaerobic layers of the plaque and are associated with cavities. Other types of bacteria (Streptococcus sanguinis) compete with S. mutans but are unable to thrive in acidic environments.

q.ex: Bacteria and fungi serve as decomposers in ecosystems, breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients back into the soil. Without decomposers, dead plants and animals would not be broken down into their chemical components like nitrogen, phosphorus, and other minerals. Grasses and other producers rely on these recycled nutrients from the soil to grow and carry out photosynthesis. While grasses produce their own energy through photosynthesis, they cannot synthesize all necessary minerals and must absorb them from the soil. Without bacteria and fungi to decompose dead organisms and return nutrients to the soil, grasses would lose this critical source of chemical components. Option i0 is correct because it accurately identifies that grasses (producers) depend on decomposers to recycle chemical nutrients from dead organisms back into a form they can absorb.

The first amino acid would be missing, but there would be no other change to the protein.
The reading frame of the sequence would shift, causing a change in the amino acid sequence after that point.

Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The deletion of the first G creates a frameshift mutation that alters how the entire sequence is read in triplet codons. The original sequence codes for amino acids in groups of three nucleotides (codons): GTT, TGT, CTG, TGG, TAC, CAC, GTG, GAC, TGA. After deleting the first G, the sequence becomes 5'-TT TGT CTG TGG TAC CAC GTG GAC TGA-3', which shifts the reading frame to: TTT, GTC, TGT, GGT, ACC, ACG, TGG, ACT, GA. This frameshift causes every codon downstream of the deletion to be read differently, producing a completely different amino acid sequence from that point forward until a stop codon is encountered. The correct answer is i3 because frameshift mutations caused by insertions or deletions that are not multiples of three nucleotides fundamentally alter the reading frame and change all subsequent amino acids in

q.s:
A widely accepted hypothesis about the origin of life on Earth is that life arose approximately 3.5 billion years ago as the result of a complex sequence of chemical reactions that took place spontaneously in Earth’s atmosphere. Another hypothesis about the origin of life suggests that life began somewhere else in the universe and arrived on Earth by chance.

Which of the following questions might scientists ask to most reliably determine if there has ever been life on Mars?

o.l: How far from Earth was Mars 3.5 billion years ago?
Is there scientific proof that Earth ever had an oxygen-free atmosphere?
Did Mars have the elements present in its atmosphere to support life?
Was there oxygen gas on Mars 3.5 billion years ago?

tg: Skill:Skill 3.A: Identify or pose a testable question based on an observation, data, or a model.
Topic:7.13: Origins of Life on Earth
Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: To determine if there has ever been life on Mars, scientists need to investigate whether Mars had the fundamental conditions necessary for life to exist. The question about whether Mars had the elements present in its atmosphere to support life directly addresses the basic chemical requirements for life, such as carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, and other essential elements. This question is more comprehensive than asking only about oxygen gas, since early life on Earth actually arose in an oxygen-free atmosphere through anaerobic processes. The distance from Earth is irrelevant to Mars's own potential for life, and Earth's atmospheric history doesn't inform us about conditions on Mars. Option i2 is correct because it asks about the foundational chemical prerequisites that would make life possible on Mars, regardless of whether that life arose independently or arrived from elsewhere.

q.s: Cortisol is a hormone produced in response to stress, including starvation, in humans. Which of the following is most likely an immediate effect of a starvation-induced increase in cortisol secretion?

o.l: Increased activation of the immune system
Increased urine production by the kidneys
Increased bone and collagen formation
Increased mobilization of fatty acids from fat cells

tg: Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: Cortisol is a glucocorticoid hormone that helps maintain blood glucose levels during stress and starvation. During starvation, the body needs alternative energy sources since glucose from food is unavailable. Cortisol promotes gluconeogenesis (glucose synthesis from non-carbohydrate sources) and stimulates lipolysis, the breakdown of triglycerides in adipose tissue into fatty acids and glycerol. These mobilized fatty acids can be used directly by tissues for energy or converted to ketone bodies, sparing glucose for the brain. Cortisol actually suppresses immune function, reduces bone formation, and has minimal direct effect on urine production. Increased mobilization of fatty acids from fat cells is correct because it directly addresses the energy deficit caused by starvation by providing an alternative fuel source.

q.s:
Ciprofloxacin is given as an antibiotic to healthy livestock to promote efficient weight gain. Strains of the bacterium Campylobacter jejuni naturally colonize the digestive tracts of livestock, and the C. jejuni can be transferred to people through the handling and consumption of contaminated meat. People infected with C. jejuni also are treated with ciprofloxacin.

Which of the following is the most likely consequence of adding ciprofloxacin to animal feed?

o.l: Naturally occurring strains of C. jejuni will reproduce more rapidly in the digestive tracts of livestock, reducing the risk of food-borne illnesses in people.
Ciprofloxacin-resistant strains of C. jejuni will have a selective advantage in the digestive tracts of livestock, increasing the risk of serious infections in people.
Ciprofloxacin-sensitive strains of C. jejuni will be consumed in meat that contains a chemical that inhibits bacterial growth, reducing the risk of food poisoning in people.
Actively growing strains of C. jejuni will metabolize the nutrients in meat produced by livestock operations, increasing the risk of protein deficiencies in people.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: When ciprofloxacin is routinely added to animal feed, it creates constant selective pressure on bacterial populations in livestock digestive tracts. Bacteria with random mutations conferring ciprofloxacin resistance will survive and reproduce while susceptible strains are killed off. Over time, resistant strains become dominant in the livestock population. When contaminated meat reaches consumers, these resistant bacteria can cause infections that no longer respond to ciprofloxacin treatment. This represents a classic example of antibiotic resistance evolution through natural selection in response to overuse of antibiotics in agriculture. Option i1 is correct because it accurately describes how selective pressure from antibiotic use favors resistant strains, creating a public health risk when the same antibiotic is needed for human treatment.

q.s: The table above shows derived characters for selected organisms. Based on the information in the table, which of the following cladograms best represents the evolutionary relationships among the organisms?
tg: Skill:Skill 4.B: Describe data from a table or graph, including- a. Identifying specific data points. b. Describing trends and/or patterns in the data. c. Describing relationships between variables.
q.ex: To construct the correct cladogram, we must identify which organisms share the most derived characters and therefore are most closely related. Fish have only jaws, making them the most basal group. Amphibians add two pairs of limbs, branching next. Mammals branch off after acquiring amniotic eggs and hair. Crocodilians and birds share the most recent common ancestor because both possess amniotic eggs, two pairs of limbs, and beta keratin scales, with birds having the additional derived character of feathers. This shared possession of beta keratin scales indicates crocodilians and birds are sister taxa, meaning they should branch from the same node with birds extending beyond crocodilians. Option i0 correctly shows this relationship with fish branching first, then amphibians, then mammals, and finally crocodilians with birds branching from the crocodilian lineage, reflecting their close evolutionary relationship.

q.s: Damaged tissue releases chemicals that activate platelets and stimulate the formation of blood clots. Which of the following statements about the activity of platelets best explains a positive feedback mechanism?

o.l: Activated platelets release chemicals that inhibit blood clot formation.
Activated platelets release signaling molecules that inhibit cell division in damaged tissue.
Activated platelets constrict the blood vessels, stopping blood flow.
Activated platelets release chemicals that activate more platelets.

tg: Skill:Skill 1.A: Describe biological concepts and/or processes.
Practice:Practice 1: Explain Biological Concepts, Processes, and Models Presented in Written Format.
q.ex: A positive feedback mechanism amplifies or enhances the original stimulus rather than counteracting it. In blood clotting, the initial release of chemicals from damaged tissue activates platelets. For this to be a positive feedback loop, the activated platelets must produce a response that further increases platelet activation, creating a cascade effect. Option i3 describes exactly this: activated platelets release chemicals that activate even more platelets, which then activate still more platelets, rapidly amplifying the clotting response. This stands in contrast to negative feedback, which would dampen the response. Option i3 is correct because it demonstrates the self-amplifying nature characteristic of positive feedback mechanisms.

q.s:
Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria. In an experiment, bacteriophages were labeled with either radioactive phosphorus or radioactive sulfur. The labeled bacteriophages were incubated with bacteria for a brief amount of time and then removed. The infected bacteria cells were found to contain significant amounts of radioactive phosphorus but not radioactive sulfur.

Based on the results of the experiment, which of the following types of molecules did the bacteriophages most likely inject into the bacteria cells?

o.l: Simple carbohydrate
Amino acid
DNA
Polypeptide

tg: Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: This question describes the classic Hershey-Chase experiment that demonstrated DNA is the genetic material. Phosphorus is found in the phosphate groups of DNA's sugar-phosphate backbone, while sulfur is found in certain amino acids that make up proteins. Since the bacteria contained radioactive phosphorus but not radioactive sulfur after infection, the bacteriophages must have injected molecules containing phosphorus but not sulfur. DNA contains phosphorus in its structure, while proteins contain sulfur in amino acids like cysteine and methionine. Carbohydrates and individual amino acids do not contain phosphorus in significant amounts and are not the genetic material viruses inject. DNA is correct because it is the phosphorus-containing molecule that bacteriophages inject into bacterial cells to hijack their cellular machinery for viral replication.

q.s: Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the results of the experiment?

o.l: Neither population grows as large when cultured together as each does when cultured separately.
P. caudatum prefers different food when cultured with P. aurelia than when cultured separately.
Competition for mates increases when the species are cultured together compared with when they are cultured separately.
Individuals of the species P. caudatum are smaller when cultured together with P. aurelia than when cultured separately.

f.c: In an investigation of interspecies competition, researchers grew the unicellular protozoan Paramecium aurelia in a 5 mL culture and Paramecium caudatum in a separate 5 mL culture. P. aurelia and P. caudatum were grown together in a third 5 mL culture. Each day a small sample of each culture was removed so the total number of individuals could be estimated, and the remainder of the population was transferred to fresh growth medium. The experimental results are represented in the graphs below.

tg: Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex:
When two species are cultured together and both achieve lower population sizes compared to when cultured separately, this indicates interspecific competition for shared resources. This is a classic demonstration of competitive exclusion or resource competition between species occupying similar ecological niches. The reduced population sizes in both species when co-cultured directly supports that neither population grows as large together as it does alone. Options involving food preference changes, mate competition, or individual size changes are not directly supported by simple population size data from competition experiments.

The correct answer is i0 because it directly describes the observed pattern of reduced population growth in both species when cultured together compared to separate cultures, which is the fundamental evidence of competitive interaction.

q.ex: To find the difference in carrying capacity between two species cultured separately, we need to identify the maximum population size each species reaches when grown alone. The carrying capacity is the plateau or asymptote of the population growth curve for each species. By examining the separate culture data, we determine the carrying capacity for species 1 and species 2. The difference is calculated by subtracting the smaller carrying capacity from the larger one. Based on the data provided, one species reaches approximately 400 individuals per 5.0 mL while the other reaches approximately 50 individuals per 5.0 mL, giving a difference of 350 individuals per 5.0 mL. Option i3 is correct because it represents the difference between the two carrying capacities when the species are cultured separately.

q.s: Which of the following statements best justifies the use of the experimental results in an investigation of interspecies competition?

o.l: When two populations use different sources of energy, one of the populations will thrive in a shared environment and the other will become extinct.
When two populations use the same sources of energy, resource availability in a shared environment limits the growth of both populations.
Because the change in entropy of a system containing two different species is always positive, populations typically grow faster in shared environments.
Because the free energy of a system containing two different species is always negative, populations that utilize similar resources cannot coexist in nature.

f.c: In an investigation of interspecies competition, researchers grew the unicellular protozoan Paramecium aurelia in a 5 mL culture and Paramecium caudatum in a separate 5 mL culture. P. aurelia and P. caudatum were grown together in a third 5 mL culture. Each day a small sample of each culture was removed so the total number of individuals could be estimated, and the remainder of the population was transferred to fresh growth medium. The experimental results are represented in the graphs below.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: Interspecies competition occurs when two populations compete for the same limited resources in a shared environment. The competitive exclusion principle states that when species compete for identical resources, neither can achieve maximum population growth because they must share those resources. Option i1 correctly describes this fundamental ecological concept: when populations use the same energy sources, resource limitation constrains both populations' growth rates. Option i0 incorrectly suggests complete extinction rather than coexistence or competitive exclusion. Options i2 and i3 misapply thermodynamic concepts (entropy and free energy) that are not directly relevant to population dynamics in competition studies. Option i1 is correct because it accurately reflects how shared resource use creates mutual growth limitations, which is the basis for studying interspecies competition experimentally.

q.s: If the mixed populations were cultured for an additional 25 days, which of the following predictions would be consistent with the data?

o.l: Both populations would stabilize at a small size.
Both populations would stabilize at a large size.
Both populations would be eliminated from the culture.
One population would stabilize at a large size, and the other population would be eliminated from the culture.

f.c: In an investigation of interspecies competition, researchers grew the unicellular protozoan Paramecium aurelia in a 5 mL culture and Paramecium caudatum in a separate 5 mL culture. P. aurelia and P. caudatum were grown together in a third 5 mL culture.
