The researcher claims that there is no selective advantage to fur color, so light and dark fur color phenotypes are present in similar frequencies in the fourth generation of this mouse population. Based on the data in Figure 1, which of the following best evaluates this null hypothesis?

o.l: The null hypothesis is rejected, because the change to a darker background color led to an increase in the dark-colored fur phenotype.
The null hypothesis is rejected, because there is no significant difference between the frequencies of the two phenotypes right after the human-caused change to the habitat in the third generation.

The null hypothesis cannot be rejected, because there is no significant difference between the frequencies of the two phenotypes right after the human-caused change to the habitat in the third generation.
The null hypothesis cannot be rejected, because the darker background color caused by the human-caused change to the habitat led to a decrease in the light fur color phenotype.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The null hypothesis states there is no selective advantage to fur color, meaning both phenotypes should remain at similar frequencies. The data clearly contradict this claim. In the first generation, light-colored fur was dominant (approximately 100 mice versus 20 with dark fur). After the habitat darkened following the second generation, the frequency of dark-colored fur increased dramatically while light-colored fur decreased proportionally. By the fourth generation, the frequencies had essentially reversed (approximately 20 light-colored versus 100 dark-colored mice). This systematic shift in phenotype frequencies following an environmental change demonstrates natural selection favoring dark fur in the darker habitat, providing strong evidence to reject the null hypothesis. The correct answer is i1 because the data show a clear selective advantage for dark-colored fur after the background color changed, directly contradicting the claim of no selective advantage.

q.s:
One of the oldest known mammalian fossils belongs to a small furry species, Hadrocodium wui, that lived 195 million years ago. For the following 100 million years, only a small number of groups of mammalian fossils are found in the fossil record. By 65 million years ago, the nonavian dinosaurs were extinct. By 55 million years ago, there were 130 mammal genera, including 4,000 different species that occupied a wide variety of habitats.

Which of the following best describes the cause of the rapid increase in the number of mammalian species between 65 and 55 million years ago?

o.l: It took over 100 million years for enough random mutations to occur in the genomes of early mammals to provide the variation needed for the observed speciation.
It took over 100 million years for the early mammals to disperse over a wide enough geographic area to allow allopatric speciation to occur.
After the dinosaur extinction, many ecological niches became available, leading to the adaptive radiation of mammals.
After the dinosaur extinction, mammal population sizes increased, allowing species to become more easily detectable in the fossil record.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The rapid increase in mammalian species between 65 and 55 million years ago occurred immediately after the extinction of nonavian dinosaurs, which eliminated major competitors and predators that had dominated terrestrial ecosystems. This extinction event opened up numerous ecological niches—different habitats, food sources, and ways of life—that were previously occupied by dinosaurs. When a group of organisms rapidly diversifies to fill many available ecological niches, this process is called adaptive radiation. The timing is critical: mammals existed for over 100 million years with limited diversity, but exploded in species number within just 10 million years after dinosaurs disappeared, indicating that ecological opportunity, not time for mutations or geographic dispersal, was the limiting factor. Option i3 correctly identifies adaptive radiation driven by newly available ecological niches as the cause of this rapid mammalian diversification.

q.s:
Female European corn borer moths (Ostrinia nubilalis) produce the sex pheromone 11−tetradecenyl acetate (11−TDA), which attracts males of their species. 11−TDA can be produced in two forms, E and Z, each with a different three-dimensional shape. Researchers have discovered two different strains of the European corn borer moth living in the same area. Females of the E strain produce primarily the E form of 11−TDA and females of the Z strain produce primarily the Z form of 11−TDA. Males of both strains are more attracted to the form of 11−TDA produced by the females of the same strain.

Which of the following best predicts a long-term effect of the differences between the E and Z strains?

o.l: The difference between the forms of the sex pheromone 11−TDA produced by E and Z strains will act as a prezygotic reproductive barrier leading to sympatric speciation.
The difference between the forms of the sex pheromone 11−TDA produced by E and Z strains will act as a postzygotic reproductive barrier, leading to allopatric speciation.
Since the E and Z strains are both part of the same species, they will produce fertile offspring, leading to a single strain that produces both forms of 11−TDA.
Since the E and Z strains are found in the same geographic area, they will hybridize, leading to a single strain that produces the dominant form of 11−TDA.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The pheromone difference creates behavioral reproductive isolation between the E and Z strains. Males preferentially respond to the pheromone form produced by females of their own strain, meaning E males are attracted to E females and Z males to Z females. This prevents mating between strains before fertilization occurs, making it a prezygotic barrier. Since both strains occupy the same geographic area, this represents sympatric speciation—the evolution of new species without geographic separation. Over time, reduced gene flow between the strains due to assortative mating will allow them to diverge genetically and potentially become separate species. Option i1 is correct because the pheromone difference acts as a prezygotic reproductive barrier that reduces interbreeding between strains living in the same location, which defines sympatric speciation.

q.s:
Humans vary in their ability to taste the bitter chemical compound phenylthiocarbamide (PTC). The taster phenotype is dominant to the nontaster phenotype. Researchers tested the PTC taster phenotype of individuals from an isolated population. In the sample, 780 individuals were able to taste PTC and 70 individuals were not able to taste PTC.

Assuming the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the frequency of the non-taster allele?

o.l: 0.08
0.29
0.41
0.71

tg: Skill:Skill 5.A: Perform mathematical calculations, including- a. Mathematical equations in the curriculum. b. Means. c. Rates. d. Ratios. e. Percentages.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: To solve this Hardy-Weinberg problem, first calculate the frequency of the homozygous recessive genotype (non-tasters). Out of 850 total individuals, 70 are non-tasters, so q² = 70/850 = 0.082. Since non-tasters must be homozygous recessive (tt), we can find the non-taster allele frequency by taking the square root: q = √0.082 = 0.286, which rounds to 0.29. The Hardy-Weinberg equation (p² + 2pq + q² = 1) allows us to work backward from phenotype frequencies to allele frequencies when the population is in equilibrium. The correct answer is 0.29 because it represents the square root of the non-taster phenotype frequency.

q.s:
Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1) is a recessive genetic disease that affects 1 in 900 individuals in a particular population. GD1 is caused by a mutation in the enzyme glucocerebrosidase.

Assuming the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, calculate the frequency of the wild-type (nonmutant) allele for the enzyme glucocerebrosidase.

o.l: 0.001
0.033
0.967
0.999

tg: Skill:Skill 5.A: Perform mathematical calculations, including- a. Mathematical equations in the curriculum. b. Means. c. Rates. d. Ratios. e. Percentages.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex:
To solve this Hardy-Weinberg problem, we need to find the frequency of the wild-type allele. Since Gaucher disease type 1 is recessive and affects 1 in 900 individuals, the frequency of the homozygous recessive genotype (q²) equals 1/900 or approximately 0.00111. To find q (the frequency of the mutant allele), we take the square root: q = √(1/900) = 1/30 ≈ 0.033. Using the Hardy-Weinberg equation p + q = 1, where p is the frequency of the wild-type allele, we calculate p = 1 - 0.033 = 0.967. 

The correct answer is 0.967 because it represents the frequency of the dominant wild-type allele (p) in a population where the recessive disease allele has a frequency of 0.033.

q.s:

Malaria is a disease that is caused by the eukaryotic parasite Plasmodium and is transmitted between individuals by the bite of infected mosquitoes. Different species of Plasmodium cause disease in different vertebrate species, but in all cases the parasite infects and destroys red blood cells. The repeated emergence of drug-resistant strains of Plasmodium parasites responsible for human infections has caused researchers to continually search for new drugs or combinations of drugs that can provide an effective treatment. A drug that has proven effective in recent years is artesunate, but now artesunate-resistant Plasmodium strains have also appeared.

Researchers investigated whether artesunate-resistant Plasmodium strains could be effectively treated by other drugs. In a mouse model of malaria, the researchers determined that a particular strain of artesunate-sensitive Plasmodium (ART-S) could be largely eliminated from the mice at a dose of 0.15 mg/kg. By repeated exposure of the artesunate-sensitive strain ART-S to increasing concentrations of artesunate, the researchers developed a Plasmodium strain that is highly resistant to artesunate (ART-R) and requires a minimum dose of 240 mg/kg to eliminate the parasites.

The researchers then compared how effectively several common antimalarial drugs eliminate the ART-S and ART-R strains in vitro. The researchers infected human red blood cells with the ART-S and ART-R Plasmodium strains and incubated the infected cells in tissue culture medium. They added serial dilutions of the drugs to replicate cultures and determined the IC50 for each drug, the concentration of the drug that reduced the parasite load in the red blood cells by 50% (Table 1).

River dolphins are morphologically distinct from other dolphins and are primarily restricted to freshwater ecosystems in Asia and South America. Determining the phylogeny of these animals based on morphology has been difficult because they have a large number of derived characters including a long, narrow rostrum (beak), a low dorsal fin, a flexible neck, and eyes that are greatly reduced. River dolphins were originally classified together based on morphology, but molecular studies have shown that they are less closely related than previously thought.

Scientists analyzed the nucleotide sequences of mitochondrial genes, including the genes for cytochrome b and two ribosomal RNAs. By combining the nucleotide sequence data with analyses of embryonic development and morphology, the scientists have proposed the phylogenetic tree shown in Figure 1. Baleen whales that are filter feeders are used as an outgroup.

q.s:
Zebra mussels, Dreissena polymorpha, were introduced into the Great Lakes on shipping vessels, first appearing in Lake St. Clair in the 1980s. Since that time, they have rapidly expanded in range, as shown in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Map showing the current range of zebra mussels in the United States

Which of the following best supports the alternate hypothesis that zebra mussels display characteristics of an invasive species?

o.l: Lacking natural predators and able to outcompete native species of mussels and other freshwater species for food, zebra mussels have experienced exponential population growth and rapid expansion into new habitats.
Since their arrival, zebra mussels have undergone rapid adaptive radiation, producing new species in many different habitats.
Throughout their current range, zebra mussels coexist with native mussel species, whose populations have been unaffected by the arrival of zebra mussels.
Zebra mussels can crossbreed with native mussels, producing hybrids that are better adapted in the range shown in Figure 1.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: Invasive species are characterized by rapid population growth, lack of natural predators, competitive advantage over native species, and expansion into new habitats. Option i1 describes all these key characteristics: exponential population growth, absence of natural predators, ability to outcompete native species for resources, and rapid habitat expansion. These traits directly support the hypothesis that zebra mussels are invasive. Option i2 incorrectly suggests adaptive radiation producing new species, which is not typical of invasive species over short timescales. Option i3 contradicts invasiveness by stating native populations are unaffected. Option i4 describes hybridization, which is not a defining characteristic of invasive species. The correct choice is i1 because it explicitly identifies the ecological disruption and rapid spread that define invasive species behavior.

q.s:
Figure 1 shows the changing pattern of human population sizes in rural and urban areas from 1960 to 2016 with regard to the global population.

 

Figure 1. Comparison of population size in urban and rural areas from 1960 to 2016

A scientist interested in investigating how human population trends might affect local animal species’ richness stipulates a null hypothesis that animal biodiversity in rural areas will be unaffected in the future by the human population trends shown in Figure 1. Which of the following would best refute this null hypothesis?

o.l: More rural areas will become available for animal habitats over time.
Urbanization causes habitat fragmentation.
Urbanization decreases the per person fossil fuel use in urban areas.
Water in urban areas is treated before it is released into the rivers that flow into rural areas.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The null hypothesis states that animal biodiversity in rural areas will be unaffected by the population trends shown, which indicate increasing urbanization (urban population surpassing rural population after 2007). To refute this hypothesis, evidence must show that urbanization does impact rural biodiversity. Habitat fragmentation occurs when continuous habitats are divided into smaller, isolated patches, which directly reduces species richness by limiting movement, gene flow, and available resources for animal populations. This process demonstrates a clear mechanism by which the urbanization trend would negatively affect rural animal biodiversity, contradicting the claim of no effect. The correct answer is i2 because habitat fragmentation provides direct evidence that urbanization impacts rural ecosystems and animal species diversity.

q.s:
Bt corn varieties are genetically modified to produce a toxin that specifically kills corn borers, a type of insect that eats and damages corn crops. Insects that are not closely related to corn borers are not affected by the toxin. Figure 1 shows the increasing production of Bt corn varieties and the change in the use of broad-spectrum pesticides that were the primary means of killing corn borers before the invention of Bt corn.

Figure 1. Relative use of pesticides on corn fields and percent of Bt corn in crops

How do the data in Figure 1 support the alternative hypothesis that increased use of Bt corn reduces the impact of corn farming on the natural environment?

o.l: The increased use of Bt corn will result in rapid mutation in corn borers.
The toxin in Bt corn kills only the corn pests, leaving other insects unharmed.
Other insect species will replace corn borers and require additional applications of insecticides.
Since Bt corn is not natural like non-Bt corn, it will not interact with the rest of the environment.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The data in Figure 1 show an inverse relationship between Bt corn adoption and broad-spectrum insecticide use. As Bt corn production increased from 1996 to 2013, insecticide application decreased dramatically, with the lines crossing around 2003. Broad-spectrum pesticides harm many non-target organisms in the environment, while the Bt toxin is specific to corn borers and closely related insects. By replacing broad-spectrum insecticides with a targeted toxin that only affects the pest species, Bt corn reduces chemical pollution and collateral damage to beneficial insects and other organisms. This specificity means fewer environmental impacts compared to traditional pesticide methods. The correct answer is that the toxin in Bt corn kills only the corn pests, leaving other insects unharmed, which directly explains how Bt corn reduces farming's environmental impact by eliminating the need for harmful broad-spectrum pesticides.

q.s:
The marine iguana, Amblyrhynchus cristatus, is endemic to the Galápagos Islands and is especially vulnerable to El Niño events. These iguanas feed on red and green algae. During an El Niño climate event, surface waters and their currents in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become significantly warmer than usual. Also during El Niño years, land masses experience increased rainfall.

A researcher suggests that El Niño conditions cause a significant decrease in the size of the Galápagos marine iguana population. Which of the following would best support this alternative hypothesis?

o.l: Increased rainfall on land leads to increased nutrient runoff into the ocean and increased food resources for marina iguanas.
Warm surface water contains fewer nutrients needed by red and green algae than cooler surface waters does.
Warm surface water shortens the incubation time of marine iguana embryos.
Cool surface water decreases the metabolic rate of marine iguanas, so they need more food to compensate for the lowered metabolic rate.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The hypothesis states that El Niño conditions cause a significant decrease in marine iguana population size. Since marine iguanas feed exclusively on red and green algae, any factor that reduces algae availability would limit the iguanas' food supply and support population decline. Option i2 establishes a causal chain: El Niño brings warm surface water, which contains fewer nutrients than cool water, thereby limiting the growth of red and green algae that the iguanas depend on for food. With reduced food availability, the iguana population would decline. This directly supports the hypothesis by connecting El Niño conditions to reduced food resources and subsequent population decrease. Option i2 is correct because it provides a mechanism linking El Niño warming to decreased algae (the iguanas' food source), which would cause population decline.

q.s: Which of the following mechanisms could most likely account for the origin of species B in Lake I?

o.l: Allopatric speciation
Directional selection
Stabilizing selection
Sympatric speciation

f.c:
Researchers were modeling the effects of repeated cycles of isolation with occasional interbreeding among five hypothetical fish species (species A, B, C, D, and E) found in two separate lakes (lakes I and II) that are occasionally joined by flooding, as shown in Figure 1. The research team indicated that species A would be considered to be the single common ancestor of species B, C, D, and E.

Figure 1. Current locations of populations of fish species A, B, C, D, and E

tg: Skill:Skill 2.B: Explain relationships between different characteristics of biological concepts or processes represented visually- a. In theoretical contexts. b. In applied contexts.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex: Without access to the referenced passage, the question asks about the origin of species B within Lake I. The key distinction is between allopatric and sympatric speciation. Allopatric speciation requires geographic isolation, where populations are physically separated and evolve independently. Sympatric speciation occurs within the same geographic area without physical barriers. Since species B originated in Lake I (a single, confined body of water), geographic isolation is unlikely. Directional and stabilizing selection are mechanisms that affect allele frequencies but do not directly explain speciation events. The correct answer is sympatric speciation because it is the mechanism that allows new species to arise within the same habitat, such as through polyploidy, sexual selection, or ecological niche differentiation within a lake ecosystem.

q.s: Which of the following data could best support the claim that species B arose from a speciation event in Lake I?

o.l: All of the fish species occupy the same niches in their respective lakes.
DNA analysis shows fewer differences between species A and species B in Lake I than between species B and the populations in Lake II.
Species A and species B have similar body shapes due to convergent evolution in their habitats.
Individuals of species A from Lake I can mate and produce viable offspring with individuals of species A from Lake II.

f.c:
Researchers were modeling the effects of repeated cycles of isolation with occasional interbreeding among five hypothetical fish species (species A, B, C, D, and E) found in two separate lakes (lakes I and II) that are occasionally joined by flooding, as shown in Figure 1. The research team indicated that species A would be considered to be the single common ancestor of species B, C, D, and E.

Figure 1. Current locations of populations of fish species A, B, C, D, and E

tg: Skill:Skill 2.B: Explain relationships between different characteristics of biological concepts or processes represented visually- a. In theoretical contexts. b. In applied contexts.
Practice:Practice 2: Analyze Visual Representations of Biological Concepts and Processes.
q.ex:
To support the claim that species B arose from a speciation event in Lake I, we need evidence showing species B is more closely related to species A in Lake I than to populations in Lake II. DNA analysis revealing fewer genetic differences between species A and B in Lake I compared to differences between species B and Lake II populations directly demonstrates this closer evolutionary relationship. Fewer DNA differences indicate more recent common ancestry, suggesting species B diverged from species A within Lake I rather than migrating from elsewhere or arising independently. This molecular evidence provides the strongest support for sympatric speciation occurring in Lake I.

The correct choice is i2 because it provides direct genetic evidence of closer evolutionary relationship between species A and B within Lake I, supporting the claim of local speciation rather than migration or independent origin.

q.s:
Commercial bananas are grown as a monoculture, with all banana plants cloned from one original banana plant. The commercial strains of bananas are seedless, so each new banana plant has to be manually planted from a cutting of an existing banana root. In the 1950s, the Gros Michel banana strain, the dominant export banana at that time, was destroyed by the fungus Fusarium oxysporum. A new Fusarium resistant variety, the Cavendish banana, was developed and is currently the banana strain grown for export. Recently, a Fusarium strain that successfully attacks the Cavendish strain has been documented.

Which of the following best provides reasoning supporting a method that would help protect commercial banana crops from infection by pathogenic organisms such as Fusarium fungi?

o.l: The commercial banana strains should be exposed to X-rays to encourage random mutations that will then be passed to offspring, producing resistance to pathogenic organisms.
The Cavendish banana plants should be exposed to pathogenic organisms under controlled conditions, so the plants can be encouraged to mutate and develop resistance to the pathogens.
The commercial banana strains should not be grown in monocultures, since many pathogenic organisms are able to evolve rapidly in response to a single selective pressure.
Growing the Cavendish strain under different conditions will allow natural selection to produce the variation needed to resist infection by pathogenic organisms.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.C: Provide reasoning to justify a claim by connecting evidence to biological theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: Commercial banana monocultures consist of genetically identical clones, meaning all plants share the same vulnerabilities to pathogens. When a pathogen like Fusarium evolves to attack one plant, it can rapidly spread through the entire crop because there is no genetic variation to provide resistance. This lack of genetic diversity creates a single selective pressure that allows pathogens to evolve quickly and devastate entire populations, as occurred with the Gros Michel strain in the 1950s. Options involving mutations are ineffective because banana plants are seedless and reproduce asexually through cuttings, so any induced mutations would not be passed to offspring. Growing diverse banana varieties instead of monocultures would provide genetic variation, making it harder for a single pathogen strain to wipe out all crops. Option i3 is correct because it identifies the fundamental problem—monoculture creates uniform selective pressure that enables rapid pathogen evolution—and implies the solution of increasing genetic diversity.

q.s:
Researchers studying the evolutionary relationships of three species of snails collected the data shown in Table 1.

Table 1. Comparison of selected characteristics of three snail species

Species A Species B Species C
Location of Fossils North America North America Europe
Shell Orientation Counterclockwise Counterclockwise Clockwise
Shell Composition Calcium Carbonate Calcium Carbonate Calcium Carbonate
Trophic Level Carnivore Carnivore Detritivore
DNA Analysis %A+T=43.2 %A+T=43.4 %A+T=43.0
%G+C=56.8 %G+C=56.6 %G+C=57.0

Which of the following data sets is most likely to provide reliable information about the evolutionary relationships among these three snail species?

o.l: Shell composition and shell orientation
Trophic level and DNA analysis
Location of fossils and shell orientation
Shell composition and location of fossils

tg: Skill:Skill 4.B: Describe data from a table or graph, including- a. Identifying specific data points. b. Describing trends and/or patterns in the data. c. Describing relationships between variables.
q.ex: To determine evolutionary relationships, researchers need characteristics that vary among species and reflect shared ancestry rather than convergent evolution or environmental adaptation. Shell composition (calcium carbonate) is identical in all three species, making it uninformative for distinguishing relationships. Trophic level can change relatively quickly through adaptation and does not necessarily reflect evolutionary history. DNA analysis shows nearly identical percentages across all species (differences of only 0.2-0.4%), providing minimal discriminatory power. In contrast, location of fossils (North America vs. Europe) and shell orientation (counterclockwise vs. clockwise) both show clear variation that distinguishes Species C from Species A and B, while grouping A and B together. These morphological and biogeographic traits are heritable and stable, making them reliable indicators of evolutionary divergence. The correct choice is correct because fossil location and shell orientation provide the most variation and phylogenetically informative data among the three species.

q.s:
Researchers observed selected internal structures of four different microscopic organisms as part of a larger study on the divergence between eukaryotes and prokaryotes. Their observations are recorded in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Selected cellular structures in four organisms

Which organism would the researchers most likely predict to be the most distantly related to eukaryotes?

o.l: Organism I
Organism II
Organism III
Organism IV

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The key distinction between prokaryotes and eukaryotes is the presence of a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Organism I contains only a single circular chromosome with no nucleus, which is characteristic of prokaryotic cells like bacteria. Organisms II and III both have nuclei with linear chromosomes and mitochondria, making them clearly eukaryotic. Organism IV shows linear chromosomes without a depicted nucleus, but linear chromosomes are a eukaryotic trait. Since the question asks which organism is most distantly related to eukaryotes, the prokaryotic Organism I would be the most distantly related due to its fundamentally different cellular organization. Organism I is correct because it displays the defining prokaryotic characteristic of lacking a nucleus and having a circular chromosome, representing the greatest evolutionary distance from eukaryotes.

q.s:
Transposable elements are significant features in the genomes of almost all eukaryotic organisms. The accumulation of these elements in various species can help determine their relatedness. Table 1 indicates the presence (+) or absence (−) of 5 segments of DNA that have been moved by transposition (transposons) in 6 primate species.

Table 1. Presence or absence of 5 transposons in primate species

Species 1 2 3 4 5
Human − + + + +

Orangutan − − − + +
Gibbon − − − − −

Which of the following best predicts how phylogenetic relationships might be revised if transposon 1 was not found in chimpanzees?

o.l: Bonobos would be more closely related to humans than to chimpanzees.
Chimpanzees would be more closely related to humans than to bonobos.
Orangutans would be more closely related to humans than to chimpanzees.
Chimpanzees would be more closely related to gibbons than to gorillas.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.E: Predict the causes or effects of a change in, or disruption to, one or more components in a biological system based on- a. Biological concepts or processes. b. A visual representation of a biological concept, process, or model. c. Data.

q.ex:
To determine phylogenetic relationships using transposons, species sharing more transposon insertions are more closely related. Currently, bonobos and chimpanzees both have all five transposons (including transposon 1), making them equally related to humans, who has four transposons (lacking only transposon 1). If transposon 1 were absent in chimpanzees, chimpanzees would then share the exact same transposon pattern as humans (lacking transposon 1 but having transposons 2-5). This would make chimpanzees and humans identical in their transposon profile, indicating they are more closely related to each other than either is to bonobos. Bonobos would still have all five transposons, making them slightly more divergent from the human-chimpanzee pair.

Choice i2 is correct because removing transposon 1 from chimpanzees creates an identical transposon pattern between chimpanzees and humans, indicating closer

q.s:
A group of biologists were investigating the effects of light color on phototropism (growing toward the light source) in tomato plants. Four groups of tomato plants were grown in the same greenhouse under identical conditions. Each group was then placed in a different room, each room having a different color of light, exposed to that single color of light from different directions for one week at a time. After each week, the biologists counted the number of tomato plants in the groups that were showing evidence of phototropism. The results are summarized in Table 1.

Table 1. Phototropic responses of plants to different colors of light

Which of the following correctly identifies the dependent and independent variables in this experiment?

o.l: The color of the light is the dependent variable, and the percentage of plants showing phototropism is the independent variable.
The percentage of plants showing phototropism is the dependent variable, and the color of the light is the independent variable.
The direction of the light is the dependent variable, and the percentage of plants showing phototropism is the independent variable.
The color of the light is the dependent variable, and the direction of the light is the independent variable.

tg: Skill:Skill 3.C: Identify experimental procedures that are aligned to the question, including- a. Identifying dependent and independent variables. b. Identifying appropriate controls. c. Justifying appropriate controls.
Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: In experimental design, the independent variable is what the researcher deliberately manipulates or changes, while the dependent variable is what is measured as a response. In this experiment, the biologists controlled and varied the color of light (red, green, blue, or white) that each group of tomato plants received. They then measured and recorded the percentage of plants showing phototropism in response to each light color. The direction of light was also varied but served as a control to ensure consistent phototropic response across all directions for each color. Since the researchers manipulated light color and measured the phototropic response, the color of light is the independent variable and the percentage of plants showing phototropism is the dependent variable. Option i2 correctly identifies these relationships.

q.s:
Quorum sensing is a form of cell-to-cell communication used by some bacterial species to regulate their behavior and population size. Staphylococcus aureus uses quorum sensing to activate its virulence genes once its population reaches a minimum size. Virulence refers to the ability of a pathogen to cause disease.

S. aureus secretes autoinducing peptide (AIP), which binds to the AgrC receptor on the bacterial cell membrane. When the S. aureus population is sufficiently large and produces enough AIP, this concentration activates AgrC and stimulates a signal cascade resulting in the production of hemolysin, a toxin used to attack the host organism. In order to lessen the impact of the toxin produced by an S. aureus infection on patients, scientists created AIP mimics intended to act as competitive inhibitors of AIP−AgrC binding at the cell surface.

Figure 1. AIP cascade producing hemolysin toxin

Identify the experimental design that would determine which AIP mimic would most effectively inhibit the production of hemolysin toxin.

o.l: Grow S. aureus in separate culture media containing one AIP mimic each and measure the amount of AIP mimic transported into the cells. The most effective AIP mimic will be absorbed the fastest.

Grow S. aureus in separate culture media containing one AIP mimic each and measure the production of hemolysin toxin. The most effective AIP mimic will be in the culture producing the lowest amount of hemolysin.
Grow S. aureus in culture media containing hemolysin and measure the production of AIP mimic in response to hemolysin intake. The most effective AIP mimic will be produced in the highest amount.

Grow S. aureus in separate culture media containing one AIP mimic each and measure the amount of live cells in each culture. The most effective AIP mimic will be the one that killed the most S. aureus.

tg: Skill:Skill 3.C: Identify experimental procedures that are aligned to the question, including- a. Identifying dependent and independent variables. b. Identifying appropriate controls. c. Justifying appropriate controls.
Practice:Practice 3: Determine Scientific Questions and Methods.
q.ex: The goal is to find which AIP mimic best inhibits hemolysin toxin production by acting as a competitive inhibitor of AIP-AgrC binding. A competitive inhibitor blocks the natural substrate (AIP) from binding to its receptor (AgrC), preventing the downstream signal cascade that leads to toxin production. To test effectiveness, the experiment must directly measure the outcome of interest: hemolysin toxin levels. Growing S. aureus in separate cultures with different AIP mimics and measuring hemolysin production allows direct comparison of each mimic's inhibitory effect. The most effective mimic will produce the lowest hemolysin levels because it most successfully blocks AIP from activating AgrC receptors. Option i2 is correct because it directly measures the target outcome (hemolysin production) and identifies the most effective inhibitor as the one producing the lowest toxin levels.

Glucose is the preferred carbon source for Escherichia coli bacteria. Researchers isolated E. coli-M, a strain of E. coli with a single mutation that inactivates a key enzyme in one of the three glycolytic pathways E. coli bacteria use to break down glucose. In an initial experiment to study the effect of the mutation on glucose utilization and ATP production by the bacteria, the researchers add 2×104 E. coli-M bacteria to 400 mL of a growth medium that contains glucose. To measure the rate of bacterial growth, they monitor the optical density of the culture as a measure of the bacterial concentration over time.

(a) Describe why monitoring the growth rate of the E. coli-M bacteria is a useful indicator of the effect of the glycolytic enzyme mutation on the bacteria.

q.s:
Students in a class were divided into five groups to analyze community structure. Each group of students assessed the species of plants in four environments and determined the Simpson's Diversity Index for each environment. The Simpson's Diversity Index takes into account the number of species present as well as the abundance of each species. The index values are shown in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Simpson's Diversity Index for four environments

Based on the data in Figure 1, which of the following statements is most accurate about the species diversity of the four different environments that the students analyzed?

o.l: The light, moist environment is the most ideal environment for plants.
The most diverse environment is the dark, dry environment because plants are best able to protect themselves from drying out during the summer months.
Based on the data, there is no statistical difference between the species diversity of plants in the light, moist environment and in the dark, moist environment.
Based on the data, there is no statistical difference between the species diversity of plants in light, dry and dark, dry environments.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.B: Use confidence intervals and/or error bars (both determined using standard errors) to determine whether sample means are statistically different.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The Simpson's Diversity Index measures species diversity, with higher values indicating greater diversity. To determine if there is a statistical difference between two environments, we examine whether their error bars overlap. The light, moist environment has a mean of approximately 0.9 with error bars from 0.8 to 0.98, while the dark, moist environment has a mean of approximately 0.795 with error bars from 0.7 to 0.89. These error bars overlap substantially in the range of approximately 0.8 to 0.89, indicating no statistically significant difference between the two environments. In contrast, the light, dry and dark, dry environments have non-overlapping error bars, indicating they are statistically different. Choice i3 is correct because the overlapping error bars between light, moist and dark, moist environments demonstrate no statistical difference in species diversity.

q.s:
Interactions among populations determine how they access resources within a community. In Costa Rica, two different species of mites, Rhinoseius colwelli and Rhinoseius richardsoni, exhibit a high degree of interspecies competition. Both mite species live within the flowers of plants, and adult male mites tend to kill mites if they belong to a different species. An experiment was carried out to determine whether these aggressive interactions have resulted in niche partitioning by R. colwelli and R. richardsoni, of different flower species, with each mite species living in different plant species. The results are summarized in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Mite Habitat Preferences

Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of the data in Figure 1 ?

o.l: R. richardsoni is found significantly more frequently on Species 4 compared to Species 3.
R. colwelli is found significantly more frequently on Species 1 compared to Species 2.
R. richardsoni is found significantly more frequently on Species 3 and Species 4 compared to Species 1 and Species 2.
R. colwelli is found significantly more frequently on Species 3 and Species 4 compared to Species 1 and Species 2.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.B: Use confidence intervals and/or error bars (both determined using standard errors) to determine whether sample means are statistically different.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: To determine the correct interpretation, we must compare mite populations across flower species and assess whether differences are significant based on the error ranges provided. For R. richardsoni, Species 3 shows approximately 62 mites and Species 4 shows approximately 78 mites, while Species 1 and Species 2 each show only about 7-8 mites. The error bars for Species 3 and 4 (±17 and ±20) do not overlap with the error bars for Species 1 and 2 (ranging from -7 to +20 and -8 to +16), indicating these differences are statistically significant. In contrast, R. colwelli shows the opposite pattern, with high numbers on Species 1 and 2 but low numbers on Species 3 and 4. This demonstrates niche partitioning where R. richardsoni preferentially inhabits Species 3 and 4 while avoiding Species 1 and 2. Option i3

q.s:
Zebra mussels are an invasive species that has become widely established throughout the United States. Figure 1 shows the percent change in the population sizes of selected groups of organisms in the Hudson River since the introduction of zebra mussels. In this study chlorophyll-containing bacteria are considered phytoplankton and all other bacteria are considered bacterioplankton.

Figure 1. Change in biomass of selected Hudson River organisms after the introduction of zebra mussels

Which of the following hypotheses about the effect of zebra mussels on the Hudson River community is best supported by the data in Figure 1 ?

o.l: Shoreline fish have replaced open water fish as top predators in a stable community.
Zebra mussels have integrated into the existing community with little effect on the community stability.
The reduction in primary productivity has resulted in an unstable community that will eventually collapse.
Bacterioplankton have replaced phytoplankton as the energy harvesters in the community.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The data shows that phytoplankton, the primary producers, declined by approximately 80 percent after zebra mussel invasion. This dramatic reduction in primary productivity cascaded through the open water habitat, causing declines of about 75 percent in native mussels, 74 percent in zooplankton, and 26 percent in open water fish. While shoreline organisms increased, these gains cannot compensate for the massive loss of the foundation of the food web. Bacterioplankton increased but are not photosynthetic (they lack chlorophyll per the passage), so they cannot replace phytoplankton as primary producers. A community that has lost 80 percent of its primary productivity cannot maintain long-term stability and is at risk of collapse. Option i3 is correct because it accurately identifies that the severe reduction in primary productivity has destabilized the community structure.

q.s:
Soluble reactive phosphate (SRP) is a term used to describe the amount of phosphate available for uptake by living things. A study of river plants species and water phosphate levels was completed in Great Britain. Recently, in a section of one of the rivers studied, a population of fennel-leaved pondweed was replaced by spiked water-milfoil, even though these two plants are associated with different environmental conditions as indicated in the table below.

Table 1. Concentrations of phosphate and river plant correlations in Britain

SRP Concentration (mg/L) Plant Species Observed
<0.1 Bog pondweed (Potamogeton polygonifolius) and river water-crowfoot (Ranunculus fluitans)
0.1−0.4 Fennel-leaved pondweed (Potamogeton pectinatus)
0.4–1.0 Yellow water-lily (Nuphar lutea) and arrowhead (Sagittarias agittifolia)
>1.0 Spiked water-milfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum)

A group of researchers suggest that the concentration of available phosphate in this particular section of the British river does not have a significant impact on which plant species grow. Alternatively, another group of researchers hypothesize that levels of available phosphate do affect which plant species grow at this location. Which of the following observations would best support this alternative hypothesis?

o.l: Reforestation efforts in Britain near this section of the river have caused changes in the plant community structure.
Increased fertilizer use near this section of the river has led to increased runoff of phosphates into the river.
Spiked water-milfoil adapted to lower phosphorous conditions has been observed to outcompete fennel-leaved pondweed in this section of the river.
Measured levels of SRP in this section of the river have remained constant over a period of time.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The alternative hypothesis states that phosphate levels affect which plant species grow in the river. According to Table 1, fennel-leaved pondweed thrives at 0.1-0.4 mg/L SRP, while spiked water-milfoil requires greater than 1.0 mg/L SRP. The question states that spiked water-milfoil replaced fennel-leaved pondweed in this river section. To support the hypothesis that phosphate levels drive this species change, evidence must show that phosphate concentrations increased from the fennel-leaved pondweed range to the spiked water-milfoil range. Option i2 provides this evidence by identifying increased fertilizer runoff as a source of elevated phosphate levels, which would explain why the plant community shifted from a species associated with lower phosphate to one associated with higher phosphate. This directly links environmental phosphate change to the observed species replacement, supporting the alternative hypothesis.

q.s:
Potatoes as a food crop originated in South America. There are over 4,000 variations of potato grown there. Potatoes were brought to Europe by Spanish colonists in the late 1500s. One variety became the chief crop grown in much of Ireland by the early 1800s. Table 1 summarizes the spread of potatoes as a food crop.

Table 1. Spread of potatoes as food crop from origin in South America

Time Period Location Number of Potato Varieties Grown (approximate)
Pre–1567 South America 4,000
1567–1800 Europe 12
1840–1850 Ireland 1

The Irish Lumper variety of potato was introduced into Ireland in the early 1800s. The Lumper soon became the only variety of potato grown in much of Ireland. The potato blight destroyed most of the Lumper crop between 1845 and 1852 resulting in the death of about 1 million Irish from starvation.

A researcher suggests that the Irish monoculture (growing a single crop) of the Lumper potato did not significantly change the overall resistance of the potato crop in Ireland to diseases. Which of the following observations best refutes this null hypothesis?

o.l: Before the arrival of the potato blight, there were already two other potato plant diseases in Ireland.
The number of fatalities from the Irish potato famine was greater than the rest of the European countries combined.
During the early nineteenth century, the vast majority of people in Ireland depended on the Lumper potato for food.
Growing more varieties of potatoes increases competition for available resources, which may yield fewer potatoes.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex:
The null hypothesis states that monoculture did not significantly change overall disease resistance. To refute this, we need evidence showing that monoculture made the crop more vulnerable to disease. Option i2 provides this evidence by comparing Ireland's famine deaths to the rest of Europe combined. Since Europe grew 12 potato varieties while Ireland grew only 1, the dramatically higher death toll in Ireland suggests that the lack of genetic diversity made the Irish crop far more susceptible to the blight. If monoculture had no effect on resistance, Ireland's losses would have been proportional to other European countries that also grew potatoes. The disproportionate devastation in Ireland directly contradicts the null hypothesis and demonstrates that monoculture reduced disease resistance.

Option i2 is correct because it provides comparative data showing Ireland suffered far worse consequences from the same disease than regions with greater crop diversity, directly refuting the claim that monoculture did not affect disease resistance.

q.s:
A study recorded changes in the distribution of some commercial marine species off the East Coast of the United States over a period of several decades. The results of the study are summarized in Figure 1.

Figure 1. Latitude that is the center of commercial harvesting of specified marine species

Some researchers link changes in the distribution of these species to warming of the oceans due to climate change. Which of the following pieces of data best supports this alternative hypothesis?

o.l: Decreased acidity of ocean water in the more southern latitudes caused a migration of these species northward.
These species evolved new adaptations over time, allowing them to survive in warmer ocean environments.
The prey of these species require colder waters to survive, and owing to warming in the oceans, they are moving farther north, to higher latitudes, where the water is colder.
Diseases devastated the prey of these species, forcing them to move northward as insufficient food was available in their original range.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The graph shows that all three commercial marine species (lobster, red hake, and summer flounder) have generally shifted their centers of commercial harvesting northward to higher latitudes over the decades from 1970 to 2010. If ocean warming due to climate change is driving this northward migration, the species would be moving to colder waters at higher latitudes. Option i3 directly supports this hypothesis by explaining that the prey of these species require colder waters and are moving north due to ocean warming, which would cause the predator species to follow their food source northward. This creates a clear causal chain: warming oceans drive prey to colder northern waters, and the commercial species follow their prey. Option i3 is correct because it provides a mechanism linking ocean warming to northward migration through the movement of prey species seeking colder waters.

q.s:
Climate change can affect oceanic ecosystems and their food webs. In the East China Sea (ECS), three major climactic events were considered:

  • the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO),
  • the East Asia winter monsoon (EAWM), and
  • the El Niño Southern Oscillation.

Figure 1 shows the relationships among these climactic events, surface sea temperature (SST), amount of phytoplankton, and copepod abundance. Copepods are important primary consumers in this ecosystem, and many species of fish depend on copepods as a food source. Solid arrows on the diagram indicate a statistical effect. The thicker the arrow, the greater the effect. Dashed arrows indicate statistically insignificant relationships.

Figure 1. Structural equation model deciphering interactions among climate, phytoplankton, and copepods in the southern East China Sea. Solid arrows indicate statistical effects, with the thickness of the arrow reflecting the relative effect. Dashed arrows indicate inconsequential effects.

What do the data in Figure 1 suggest about a null hypothesis that the East China Sea ecosystem is unaffected by climactic events?

o.l: The null hypothesis is rejected since there are statistical effects of EAWM and PDO on surface sea temperature and copepod abundance.
The null hypothesis is rejected because the El Niño Southern Oscillation has a statistical impact on the abundance of copepods in the ECS.
The null hypothesis is rejected because the EAWM and PDO do not have statistical effects on the abundance of copepods and phytoplankton in the ECS.
The null hypothesis is rejected because the El Niño Southern Oscillation does not have a statistical impact on the abundance of copepods in the ECS.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: The null hypothesis states that the East China Sea ecosystem is unaffected by climactic events. To reject this hypothesis, we need evidence that climactic events DO have statistical effects on the ecosystem. Figure 1 shows solid arrows (indicating statistical significance) from EAWM to both SST and copepods, and from PDO to both SST and copepods. These solid arrows demonstrate that two climactic events have measurable impacts on key ecosystem components. Since copepods are described as important primary consumers that many fish depend on, and SST affects phytoplankton which affects copepods, these statistical relationships prove the ecosystem is indeed affected by climate. The null hypothesis is therefore rejected because EAWM and PDO show significant effects on surface sea temperature and copepod abundance.

q.s:
Hemoglobin is a highly conserved protein used by all mammals to transport oxygen. Table 1 was constructed by comparing the amino acid sequence in the hemoglobin molecules from five different mammal species.

Table 1. Hemoglobin amino acid differences among five different mammal species

Species 1 Species 2 Species 3 Species 4 Species 5
Species 1 – 21 11 13 5
Species 2 – 18 17 20
Species 3 – 3 10
Species 4 – 12
Species 5 –

Which of the following best describes the importance of the number of amino acid differences indicated in Table 1 ?

o.l: They reflect the different environments where the organisms were captured.
They reflect the number of base pair changes in the DNA.
They reflect random changes due to translation errors.
They reflect the number of oxygen molecules each hemoglobin molecule carries.

tg: Skill:Skill 4.B: Describe data from a table or graph, including- a. Identifying specific data points. b. Describing trends and/or patterns in the data. c. Describing relationships between variables.
q.ex: The table shows amino acid differences in hemoglobin sequences between five mammal species. Each amino acid in a protein is encoded by a codon (three DNA base pairs), so differences in amino acid sequences directly result from changes in the underlying DNA sequence. These differences accumulate over evolutionary time through mutations in the DNA that codes for hemoglobin. The greater the number of amino acid differences between two species, the more DNA mutations have occurred since they shared a common ancestor. Environmental factors do not directly change amino acid sequences, translation errors are typically corrected and not heritable, and oxygen-carrying capacity is determined by hemoglobin structure rather than sequence variation between species. The correct answer is that amino acid differences reflect base pair changes in the DNA because mutations in DNA codons are what produce different amino acids in the protein sequence.

q.s:
In an experiment, three different animals were exposed to a series of environmental temperatures and their body temperatures were assessed at multiple temperature points between 10 and 40 degrees Celsius. Ten different individuals of each type of animal were included in the study to produce an average body temperature profile for each type of animal. Figure 1 shows the data collected.

Figure 1. Effect of environmental temperature on body temperature of selected animals

Which of the following statements is most consistent with the data in Figure 1 ?

o.l: Armadillos tend to be more metabolically active than either gerbils or snakes are.
Armadillos cannot survive at environmental temperatures over 30°C.
Snakes are found in terrestrial rather than aquatic environments.
Snakes display behaviors that allow them to absorb or radiate heat as required.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The graph shows that gerbils and armadillos maintain relatively constant body temperatures across varying environmental temperatures, indicating they are endotherms (warm-blooded). In contrast, the snake's body temperature closely tracks environmental temperature, rising from 15°C to 40°C as the environment warms, which is characteristic of ectotherms (cold-blooded). Since ectotherms cannot internally regulate body temperature through metabolism alone, they must rely on behavioral thermoregulation such as basking in sunlight to absorb heat or seeking shade to cool down. The data provides no information about metabolic activity levels, survival limits, or habitat preferences. Option i4 is correct because snakes, as ectotherms shown by their temperature-dependent body temperatures, must use behavioral mechanisms to regulate their body temperature by absorbing or radiating heat.

q.s:
In an experiment to determine the effect of light availability on species richness in an environment, a grassland was divided into 26 plots that were assigned to one of two treatment groups:

1. Clipped – plots were mowed to simulate the grazing of herbivores that maintain the low height of grasses.

2. Enclosure – plots were enclosed in fences, and grasses were allowed to grow undisturbed to their maximum height.

After eight years, data was collected on the amount of light penetration to the soil (bottom light density) and the number of species in the two treatment groups. Figure 1 shows the averaged light penetration measurements, and Figure 2 shows the averaged number of species per plot type.

Figure 1. Average bottom light intensity in clipped plots versus enclosed plots

Figure 2. Richness comparison of two treatments

Which of the following statements is consistent with the data shown in the figures?

o.l: Grazing activity in a field decreases the species richness of the field.
Different patterns of energy availability in ecosystems will affect species richness.
Forests that develop a closed canopy with a shaded floor will exhibit increased species richness.
The enclosed plots are more efficient at capturing and distributing energy than the clipped plots.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The data show that clipped plots (simulating grazing) have lower bottom light density (170 W/m²) but higher species richness (17 species) compared to enclosed plots (500 W/m² light but only 11.6 species). This demonstrates that different light availability patterns—a form of energy availability—correlate with different levels of species richness. Option i1 is incorrect because grazing (clipping) actually increased species richness. Option i3 contradicts the data since the enclosed plots with reduced light at ground level had lower species richness. Option i4 makes an unsupported claim about energy capture efficiency that cannot be determined from species counts and light measurements alone. Option i2 is correct because it accurately generalizes that varying energy availability (light penetration) affects species richness, as demonstrated by the inverse relationship shown in the figures.

q.s:
Figure 1 shows the population fluctuations of phytoplankton and zooplankton in the eastern Pacific Ocean over the course of six years. The major dip in phytoplankton was attributed to a lack of nutrients for phytoplankton.

Figure 1. Relative abundance of plankton over time in the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean

Of the following, which explains why the zooplankton also dipped during the same year and then seemed to cycle over the next three years?

o.l: The zooplankton rely on the same nutrients for energy harvesting as the phytoplankton, so their population was also unable to acquire the necessary energy to maintain their population level. After that major dip there were enough nutrients for both categories of plankton.

Zooplankton are more temperature-sensitive than the phytoplankton, so the annual seasonal changes will affect their population sizes in a cyclical fashion. There was a sudden, extreme temperature change in the first dip that also affected the phytoplankton.
A migration of whales was blown off course by a storm one year and ate most of the phytoplankton and zooplankton. In the following years the whales returned to their normal migration route.

The reduction in the phytoplankton population meant that the zooplankton’s energy source was drastically reduced, leading to the decrease in the zooplankton population size. After the dip, the phytoplankton provided a steady energy source, and the zooplankton population fluctuated around its carrying capacity.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The zooplankton population decline follows the phytoplankton decline because zooplankton are consumers that feed on phytoplankton as their primary energy source. When phytoplankton populations dropped due to nutrient deficiency in 1998, zooplankton lost their food supply, causing their population to crash as well. After phytoplankton recovered and stabilized, the zooplankton population fluctuated around a relatively stable level, which represents typical population dynamics near carrying capacity when resources are adequate. This predator-prey relationship explains the lagged response of zooplankton to phytoplankton changes. Option 4 is correct because it accurately describes the trophic relationship between phytoplankton (producers) and zooplankton (primary consumers) and explains both the initial decline and subsequent stabilization with normal population fluctuations.

q.s:
Phytoplankton (dashed line) are important because they occupy the bottom of the food web absorbing CO2, functioning as a carbon sink. A scientist suggests that an El Niño event in early 1998 caused a significant decrease in the abundance of phytoplankton that year in the equatorial Pacific Ocean.

Figure 1. Relative abundance of plankton over time in the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean

Which of the following observations would best support this alternative hypothesis?

o.l: Previous dips in plankton abundance coincided with other El Niño events.
Primary consumers also experienced a dip in abundance in early 1998.
After mid-1998, there is no correlation between phytoplankton and zooplankton abundance.
CO2 levels in surface waters increased significantly in this region during 1998.

tg: Skill:Skill 5.D: Use data to evaluate a hypothesis (or prediction), including- a. Rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis. b. Supporting or refuting the alternative hypothesis.
Practice:Practice 5: Perform Statistical Tests and Mathematical Calculations to Analyze and Interpret Data.
q.ex: To support the hypothesis that an El Niño event caused the 1998 phytoplankton decline, the best evidence would establish a consistent pattern linking El Niño events to phytoplankton decreases. If previous dips in plankton abundance coincided with other El Niño events, this demonstrates a reproducible cause-and-effect relationship rather than a single coincidental occurrence. This pattern strengthens the claim that El Niño specifically drives phytoplankton decline. Option i2 describes a consequence of phytoplankton decline but does not establish El Niño as the cause. Option i3 discusses post-1998 correlation patterns unrelated to causation. Option i4 would actually contradict the hypothesis since increased CO2 availability typically supports phytoplankton growth. Choice i1 is correct because demonstrating repeated correlation between El Niño events and phytoplankton dips provides the strongest support for a causal relationship.

q.s:
In a study of energy flow, the following data were collected:

  • Each human requires 55 grams of protein per day.
  • An acre of soybeans produces 200,000 grams of protein per year.
  • A cow grazing on one acre of land produces 19,000 grams of protein per year.

Based on these data, an acre of land would support:

  • 10 humans per year on a diet of soy, or
  • 0.9 human per year on a diet of beef.

Which of the following statements best explains these relationships in terms of energy transfer?

o.l: Humans are better adapted to make efficient use of soy protein than beef protein, so they can extract more energy from a gram of soy protein than from a gram of beef protein.
A cow can harvest energy only at a certain rate, so adding another cow to the acre of land would double the number of humans supported by the acre.
Preparing meat for human consumption takes more energy per gram of protein than preparing soy for consumption.
Only 10% of the energy on each level of the trophic pyramid is available for use by the next level. The rest is lost as heat or used for growth and repair.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The key to this problem is understanding energy transfer efficiency in food chains. When humans eat soybeans directly, they are primary consumers obtaining energy from producers. When humans eat beef, they are secondary consumers, with cows as an intermediate step. At each trophic level, approximately 90% of energy is lost to metabolic processes, heat, and growth, leaving only about 10% available to the next level. The data support this: an acre produces 200,000 grams of soy protein supporting 10 humans, but when that same acre feeds cows first, only 19,000 grams of beef protein are produced, supporting 0.9 humans—roughly 10% as efficient. This demonstrates the 10% rule of ecological energy transfer between trophic levels. Option i4 is correct because it accurately explains that energy loss at each trophic level accounts for the dramatic difference in how many humans can be supported by direct plant consumption versus consumption through an animal intermediary.

q.s:
The deep ocean floor communities contain very little life. In constant darkness, the water at these depths hovers around 2°C. Sparsely distributed in this environment are hydrothermal vent ecosystems. Superheated water streams out of the vents at temperatures approaching 400°C. These waters are rich in inorganic materials, including carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide. Hydrothermal vent zones have a density of organisms 10,000 to 100,000 times greater than found on the surrounding seafloor.

Scientists have studied these vents to determine the energy source for these communities and the identity of the primary producers in the perpetual darkness of the ocean floor. As expected, they found a total absence of photosynthetic organisms at all vents, identifying mats of bacteria as the producers of the carbon compounds that are used by the rest of the community for growth, repair, and as an energy source.

Which of the following describes how the vent bacteria harvest energy to produce organic compounds for use by the vent community?

o.l: The bacteria use the heat from the hot water to assemble carbon-based materials from inorganic molecules.
The bacteria function as chemoautotrophs, extracting energy from hydrogen-rich inorganic molecules.
Organic matter drifting down from the ocean’s surface is used to make molecules with enough energy to sustain the vent community.
The bacteria can recycle the energy from the waste products and dead material produced by the heterotrophs of the vent community into energy-rich carbon compounds that can be recycled.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The passage establishes that hydrothermal vent bacteria are the primary producers in an environment with no light and abundant inorganic materials like carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide. Since photosynthesis is impossible without light, these bacteria must use an alternative energy source. Chemoautotrophs are organisms that obtain energy by oxidizing inorganic compounds, particularly hydrogen-rich molecules like hydrogen sulfide, to synthesize organic compounds from carbon dioxide. This process, called chemosynthesis, allows the bacteria to convert chemical energy from inorganic molecules into organic matter that supports the entire vent community. Option i2 correctly identifies the bacteria as chemoautotrophs that extract energy from hydrogen-rich inorganic molecules, which aligns with the presence of hydrogen sulfide in the vent waters and the absence of photosynthetic organisms.

Caenorhabditis elegans is an approximately 1 mm long nematode (worm) that lives in the soil and eats bacteria such as Pseudomonas. Scientists have determined that when C. elegans is hunting for food, the worms have different patterns of movement that depend on the location and quality of the food source. Scientists hypothesized that C. elegans might be attracted to certain chemicals produced by Pseudomonas. They tested this hypothesis by placing 100 C. elegans in the center of each of a series of petri dishes containing a layer of agar over which the worms could move. A drop of a test chemical diluted in ethanol was placed at one edge of each dish and an equal-sized drop of ethanol was placed at the opposite edge of the dish. The scientists determined the number of worms to reach each spot over a period of time.

(a) Describe why the location and quality of food sources in the soil are sometimes likely to stimulate random movements by C. elegans, but at other times are more likely to stimulate directed movements.

Skill:Skill 6.B: Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and/or data.

Skill:Skill 3.C: Identify experimental procedures that are aligned to the question, including- a. Identifying dependent and independent variables. b. Identifying appropriate controls. c. Justifying appropriate controls.
Skill:Skill 3.B: State the null and alternative hypotheses or predict the results of an experiment.

q.s:
Baker’s yeast, Saccharomycetes cerevisiae, is the species of yeast that is commonly used in baking, brewing, and making wine. It is a single-celled organism; each cell is capable of undergoing asexual reproduction by mitosis and sexual reproduction by meiosis, forming spores that combine with other spores.

To find out if energy and nutritional resource availability determines which form of reproduction is used, researchers grew twenty yeast colonies on an agar medium plate providing ideal nutrient environments. Each colony was composed of a population of yeast that originated from a single yeast cell that had reproduced asexually to form a population of millions of yeast clones. That plate was used to produce replicate plates of yeast colonies. Each replicate plate was a mirror image of the original cultures, so each colony could be subjected to each treatment group. The replicate plates contained different media as follows.

  • Robust media: Contains all nutrients required by yeast in excess amounts
  • Complete media: Contains all nutrients at a level promoting exponential growth at rmax⁡
  • Minimal media: Nutrients available at a low level, allowing growth, but stressing the yeast colonies
  • Deficient media: Nutrient content less than what is needed to sustain growth, extreme stress on yeast colonies

Eight replica plates were made, two plates of each media, and all plates were incubated at 30°C for 24 hours. Yeast from each colony were observed through a microscope and their means of reproduction determined. Table 1 summarizes these results.

Table 1: Reproductive Strategy of S. cerevisiae under different environmental stress levels (20 different colonies per medium ×2)

Medium Nutritional Conditions Colonies Reproducing Sexually Colonies Reproducing Asexually Colonies Showing No Reproduction
Robust Ideal 0 38 2
Complete Adequate 2 35 3
Minimal Mild Stress 24 13 3
Deficient Extreme Stress 28 1 11

Which of the following best explains the data in Table 1 ?

o.l: All forty colonies are genetically identical. Differences in stress responses are due to experimental error.
Asexual reproduction allows stressed colonies to divide rapidly and compete for limited resources with other colonies.
Mild nutritional stress does not trigger a change in reproductive strategy among yeast cultures.
Yeast respond to nutritional stress with sexual reproduction, producing new genetic combinations, or dormancy.

tg: Skill:Skill 6.D: Explain the relationship between experimental results and larger biological concepts, processes, or theories.
Practice:Practice 6: Develop and Justify Scientific Arguments Using Evidence.
q.ex: The data show a clear shift in reproductive strategy as nutritional stress increases. Under ideal and adequate conditions (robust and complete media), yeast predominantly reproduce asexually (38/40 and 35/40 colonies respectively). As stress increases to mild levels (minimal media), sexual reproduction becomes more common (24/40 colonies). Under extreme stress (deficient media), sexual reproduction dominates (28/40 colonies) while many colonies become dormant (11/40 showing no reproduction). This pattern indicates that yeast switch from asexual reproduction in favorable conditions to sexual reproduction or dormancy under stress. Sexual reproduction generates genetic diversity through meiosis and recombination, which may help offspring survive variable or harsh environments. Option i4 is correct because it accurately describes both the stress-induced shift to sexual reproduction (which creates new genetic combinations) and the increased dormancy observed under extreme nutritional stress.
